new_roles.description:
**Universal Ingredients**

*Innovative Plant-Based Solutions for Global Industries*

Universal Ingredients is a global supplier of high-quality, plant-based specialty ingredients for human and pet consumption. With thousands of products and global sourcing capabilities, we provide customized, value-added solutions – including fruit and vegetable juices and concentrates, dehydrated ingredients, botanical extracts, flavors, and beverage systems – for food and beverage manufacturers worldwide.

Our advanced production capabilities, including aseptic beverage processing and flexible packaging solutions, enable safe, shelf-stable products with no preservatives. At the heart of our innovation is our Application Capabilities Lab, where food science experts collaborate with customers to develop market-ready solutions through product development, flavor analysis, sensory testing, and commercialization support.

Driven by innovation, sustainability, and partnership, Universal Ingredients helps customers stay ahead of evolving consumer preferences while delivering consistent quality, functionality, and performance across global markets.

Disclaimer: Shank’s Extracts manufactures various products that identify as major food allergens (milk, eggs, tree nuts, wheat, and soybeans) as well as several other food ingredients. We cannot guarantee you will not be exposed to skin and/or odor contact with these various ingredients. Your health and safety are our number one priority, and we will do our best to accommodate within reason.

**Summary**

Universal Ingredients is seeking a **Food Safety & Quality Director** to lead our Quality, Food Safety, and Regulatory functions. This leader will establish and strengthen quality systems across the organization, ensure regulatory and food safety compliance, and partner closely with Operations, Commercialization, R&D, Procurement, and Commercial teams.

The ideal candidate combines strong technical expertise with practical manufacturing leadership and has a track record of building a **preventive, accountable quality culture** focused on getting things right the first time.

**What You'll Be Doing (Essential Duties)**

* Lead the overall **Quality, Food Safety, and Regulatory strategy** for Universal Ingredients.
* Establish consistent quality standards, systems, policies, and performance expectations across the organization.
* Ensure compliance with applicable **FDA, FSMA, GMP, HACCP, SQF/GFSI, labeling, and customer requirements**.
* Strengthen **root-cause analysis, CAPA, change control, SOP/SSOP, and audit processes**.
* Partner with Operations to improve **first-pass quality** and reduce complaints, deviations, holds, rework, and recurring quality issues.
* Lead customer complaint management, regulatory inspections, certification audits, and customer audits.

new_roles.title: VP of Production
new_roles.description:
**VP of Production**
--------------------

**Location:** Los Angeles, Detroit, or San Francisco 
**Employment:** Full time, in person 
**Base salary:** $200,000–$350,000 annually

American factories deserve a supply chain that moves as fast as they do. Nox Metals is building it, along with the tools that run it. We’re a technology company supplying raw metal to frontier American manufacturers. We use software and automation to supply metal to factories faster than the industry thought possible.

### **The role**

We’re hiring a VP of Production to lead manufacturing performance across Nox Metals’ facilities. You will own how work moves through our factories: production planning, daily execution, capacity, staffing, quality, productivity, and on-time delivery.

This is a hands-on manufacturing leadership role with real time on the factory floor. You will develop production leaders, resolve constraints, and create repeatable ways of working that help teams deliver as demand grows. Success means safe, reliable production and clear accountability from the daily schedule through completed customer orders.

### **You will**

* Lead production execution across facilities, with clear expectations for safety, quality, output, cost, and delivery.
* Translate demand into practical production, staffing, shift, and capacity plans.
* Develop plant and production leaders who take ownership of results and build strong teams.
* Establish daily operating reviews, shift handoffs, escalation paths, and performance measures that drive action.
* Identify bottlenecks, reduce downtime and rework, and improve material flow and labor productivity.
* Build consistent training, work instructions, and qualification standards while staying close to how work happens.
* Protect material traceability and quality throughout production.
* Partner with maintenance and engineering on equipment reliability, capacity improvements, and automation.
* Work with supply chain and commercial teams to align material availability, production commitments, and customer needs.
* Partner with finance on production economics and equipment investment decisions.
* Help new or expanded facilities establish reliable production and sustain performance as they ramp.

### **You are**

* A manufacturing leader with a record of improving factory performance and developing accountable leaders.
* Experienced managing production teams, schedules, equipment constraints, and competing priorities.
* Uncompromising about safety, quality, and traceability.
* Fluent in capacity, throughput, labor productivity, downtime, and delivery performance.
* Comfortable making decisions on the floor and following through until problems are resolved.
* Practical, direct, and interested in improving manufacturing with software and automation.

### **Nice to have**

Experience leading multiple facilities, scaling production through rapid growth, or working in metals, machining, aerospace, industrial distribution, or related environments.

Expect regular time at our manufacturing facilities and travel between sites as needed.

Nox Metals is an equal opportunity employer. We hire based on skill, attitude, and fit for the work, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, height, weight, marital status, or any other protected status under federal, state, or local law.

We will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records in a manner consistent with the Los Angeles Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance, and the California Fair Chance Act.

Compensation Range: $200K - $350K

new_roles.title: Plant Manager - Manufacturing Operations
new_roles.description:
**Plant Manager – Manufacturing**

**The Opportunity**

We are seeking an experienced Plant Manager to lead an established, mid-size manufacturing operation in Holt, Michigan. This is an opportunity for a well-rounded manufacturing leader to take ownership of the facility's overall business performance, providing strategic direction and leadership while driving operational excellence, profitability, and continued growth.

Reporting to the VP of Operations, the Plant Manager will have full responsibility for the facility's operational and financial performance, including full P&L accountability. This individual will oversee all aspects of the business, lead and develop the management team, and ensure the facility consistently achieves its financial, operational, quality, safety, and customer objectives.

**What We're Looking For**

We are looking for a seasoned manufacturing leader who understands how to run a plant as a business. The ideal candidate brings a strong combination of operational expertise, financial acumen, and business leadership, with a proven ability to translate company objectives into measurable results.

This person will be comfortable leading through department managers, establishing accountability, making sound business decisions, and developing a culture of continuous improvement. Equally important is the ability to balance the bigger picture with an understanding of what is happening on the plant floor.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Assume full ownership and accountability for the facility's overall performance, including P&L, profitability, operating costs, and financial results.
* Develop and execute annual operating plans, budgets, and business strategies aligned with company objectives.
* Monitor financial and operational performance, analyze results, identify areas of opportunity, and implement corrective actions as needed.
* Provide leadership and oversight across all plant functions, including production, quality, maintenance, materials, shipping, and safety.
* Lead, mentor, and develop the management team, establishing clear expectations, accountability, and performance standards.
* Provide direction and oversight to the Production Manager and other functional leaders, ensuring alignment across departments and consistent execution of business objectives.
* Drive improvements in productivity, labor efficiency, throughput, quality, on-time delivery, and overall operating costs.
* Identify and implement cost-reduction initiatives, process improvements, and operational efficiencies that positively impact the bottom line.
* Maintain strong customer relationships, ensuring customer requirements are met and issues are addressed promptly and effectively.
* Oversee workforce planning, staffing, employee development, and organizational effectiveness.
* Ensure a safe working environment and maintain compliance with applicable safety regulations, quality standards, and other requirements.
* Direct capital planning and investment decisions, evaluating equipment, technology, and facility improvements to support business needs and long-term growth.
* Establish and monitor key performance indicators, using data and financial reporting to measure results and drive continuous improvement.
* Partner with senior leadership to communicate facility performance, address business challenges, and identify opportunities for growth and improvement.

**Qualifications**

* Progressive leadership experience in a manufacturing environment, with demonstrated success managing an entire plant or manufacturing operation.
* Previous full P&L responsibility, including budgeting, financial reporting, cost management, and profitability.
* Broad understanding of manufacturing operations, including production, quality, maintenance, materials management, and supporting functions.
* Proven ability to improve financial and operational performance through effective planning, execution, and accountability.
* Experience leading and developing department managers and supervisors, with the ability to build a strong, effective leadership team.
* Strong business and financial acumen, with the ability to understand financial statements, evaluate operating costs, and make sound business decisions.
* Demonstrated success with continuous improvement, process optimization, and cost-reduction initiatives.
* Strong customer-facing skills and the ability to develop and maintain productive business relationships.
* Excellent leadership, communication, organizational, and problem-solving abilities.
* A hands-on, approachable leadership style combined with the ability to think strategically and lead at the business level.

**The Opportunity**

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced manufacturing leader to take ownership of an established operation and make a meaningful impact on its overall performance and continued success. The right individual will have the opportunity to influence the business, develop a strong team, and drive improvements across all areas of the facility.

The company offers a competitive compensation package, bonus potential, and a comprehensive benefits program including health, dental, vision, 401(k), and paid time off.

This is an on-site leadership position in Holt, Michigan.

Thank you for considering this opportunity.

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Health insurance
* Paid time off
* Retirement plan

Experience:

* Plant management: 4 years (Preferred)
* P&L responsibility: 4 years (Preferred)
* composite, paint finish, or similar: 2 years (Preferred)

Work Location: In person

new_roles.title: Senior Consultant, Quality (VP-Level)
new_roles.description:
This individual will serve as an integral consultant with exposure to multiple facets of business operations. The **Senior Consultant, Quality** will be responsible for helping to set strategic direction and operational oversight of the quality function addressing all aspects of GXP compliance.This consultant ensures all internal processes and external partnerships strictly adhere to global regulatory standards, including FDA, EMA, and ICH guidelines.

**This role can be up to 10 hours per week to start.**

 

Elicio (ELTX) is a growing organization based out of the Seaport area of Boston, Massachusetts with additional staff functioning in a virtual based environment from the Greater Boston area and throughout the United States.

 

**Key Responsibilities Include**

 

* **Strategic Leadership:**Develop and execute a comprehensive quality and compliance vision that aligns with the company’s clinical and commercial objectives.
* **Quality Management System (QMS):**Design, implement, and maintain a robust QMS—including document control, change management, and CAPA (Corrective and Preventive Action) systems—that scales with the company's growth.
* **GxP Compliance Oversight:**Ensure full compliance across all GxP areas, including Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP), Good Clinical Practices (GCP), and Good Laboratory Practices (GLP).
* **Regulatory Interaction:**Serve as the primary liaison for regulatory health authorities during inspections and audits; lead the strategy for inspection readiness.
* **External Partner Management:**Oversee quality at external vendors, including contract manufacturing organizations (CMOs) and clinical research organizations (CROs), ensuring consistent quality standards and negotiating quality agreements.
* **Product Disposition:**Hold ultimate accountability for the review and release (disposition) of raw materials, intermediates, and final drug products for both clinical trials and commercial sale.
* **Culture & Talent:**Build and mentor a high-performing quality organization while championing a "Quality First" culture across all departments.

 

**Education & Professional Experience**

 

* Bachelor’s degree in a scientific or technical discipline (e.g., Biology, Chemistry, Pharmacy) is required. An advanced degree (MS, PhD, or MBA) is strongly preferred.
* 15+ years of progressive leadership in quality within the biotech or pharmaceutical industry.
* Deep knowledge of global regulatory frameworks (FDA 21 CFR Part 11, 210/211, and ISO standards) and experience in biologics or small molecule manufacturing, and parenteral products. Experience with peptide-based vaccines is a plus.
* Proven track record of managing outsourced operations successfully leading organizations through regulatory inspections and commercial product launches.
* Must thrive in a fast-paced innovative start-up environment.
* Exceptional communication and negotiation skills for interacting with executive teams and regulatory agencies.
* Strong risk management and analytical problem-solving abilities.
* Strategic thinking with a "hands-on" approach to building quality organizations and quality systems.

 

**Working Model**

**Weekly hours:** This role can be up to 10 hours per week to start. It may increase or decrease over time.

**Working Conditions:** Busy home office/office/laboratory environment with frequent deadlines and interruptions.

**Travel:** Travel may be required to the Company’s headquarters a few times per year, if necessary.

**Physical Requirements:** Subject to periods of sitting or standing, vision is required to monitor data.

**Work Location:** Hybrid preference but will consider remote

**About Elicio Therapeutics**

Elicio Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: ELTX) is a clinical-stage biotechnology company advancing a pipeline of novel lymph node-targeted immunotherapies for the treatment of some of the most aggressive cancers. By combining expertise in immunology and immunotherapy, Elicio is harnessing the natural power of the immune system with the AMP technology, which allows for therapeutic payloads to be delivered directly to the lymph nodes, with the goal of enhancing the immune system’s cancer-fighting capabilities. By targeting cancer immunotherapies to the core of the immune response, AMP aims to optimize the lymph nodes’ natural ability to educate, activate and amplify cancer-specific T cells, which are essential for recognizing and eliminating tumor cells. Engineered to synchronize immunity in these highly potent sites, AMP is built to enhance the magnitude, potency, quality and durability of the immune response to drive antitumor activity. The Company’s R&D pipeline includes off-the-shelf therapeutic cancer vaccines ELI-002, (targeting mKRAS-driven cancers) as well as ELI-007 and ELI-008 (targeting BRAF-driven cancers and p53 hotspot mutations, respectively). For more information, please visit www.elicio.com.

**About the Amphiphile Platform**

 

Elicio Therapeutics’ proprietary Amphiphile (“AMP”) platform delivers investigational immunotherapeutics directly to the “brain center” of the immune system – the lymph nodes. Elicio believes this site-specific delivery of disease-specific antigens, adjuvants and other immunomodulators may efficiently educate, activate, and amplify critical immune cells, potentially resulting in induction and persistence of potent adaptive immunity required to treat many diseases. In preclinical models, Elicio has observed lymph node-specific engagement driving therapeutic immune responses of increased magnitude, function and durability. Elicio believes our AMP lymph node-targeted approach will produce superior clinical benefits compared to immunotherapies that do not engage the lymph nodes based upon preclinical studies. Elicio’s AMP platform, originally developed at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology has broad potential in the cancer space to advance a number of development initiatives through internal activities, in-licensing arrangements or development collaborations and partnerships. The AMP platform has been shown to deliver immunotherapeutics directly to the lymph nodes by latching on to the protein albumin, found in the bloodstream, as it travels to lymphatic tissue. In preclinical models, Elicio has observed lymph node-specific engagement driving immune responses of increased magnitude, function and durability.

new_roles.title: Director Factory of the Future
new_roles.description:
**Company Description**

**About AbbVie**

AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at www.abbvie.com. Follow @abbvie on LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram, X and YouTube.

 **Job Description**

The Director, Factory of the Future, leads AbbVie’s global strategy, design standards, and delivery of next-generation factories and manufacturing operations that leverage Industry 4.0/5.0, robotics, automation, and AI. The Director owns the Factory of the Future vision and roadmap across biotechnology, aseptic manufacturing, packaging, medical device, and chemical production, and leads a team of senior engineers and technical leaders who develop reference designs, run pilots, and enable deployment into new facilities and major site transformations. This role partners with Operations leadership, Engineering, Quality, PDS&T, Supply Chain, BTS, and Security to ensure future factories are safe, compliant, flexible, and highly automated, and deliver measurable gains in quality, speed, and cost.

**Vision and Strategy**

* **Factory of the Future strategy:** Define and own the multi-year Factory of the Future vision, technology roadmap, and investment case, aligned to Operations, network, and enterprise AI and digital strategies.
* **Network and capital alignment:** Partner with Global Engineering, Manufacturing, and Finance to embed future-factory design principles and technology choices into the capital plan, site master plans, and new-facility business cases.

**Design and Technology Leadership**

* **Reference designs and standards:** Establish global reference designs, design standards, and technology platforms for aseptic and biologics manufacturing, packaging, device assembly, and chemical production, including modular, flexible, and continuous concepts.
* **Automation, robotics, and AI:** Direct the evaluation, piloting, and scale-up of robotics, autonomous material handling, vision inspection, digital twins, advanced process control, and AI-enabled operations, in partnership with BTS and Operations AI.
* **Technical governance:** Provide design authority and review for major capital projects; ensure cGMP, Annex 1, data integrity, device regulations, EHS, and OT/IT cybersecurity requirements are built in from concept stage.

**Delivery and Value**

* **Portfolio delivery:** Lead a portfolio of Factory of the Future pilots, proofs of concept, and project deployments, managing scope, schedule, budget, risk, and benefits.
* **Value tracking:** Define KPIs (e.g., OEE, right-first-time, labor productivity, cycle time, capex efficiency, sustainability) and report realized value to the Operations Leadership Team.

**Leadership and Ecosystem**

* **Team leadership:** Build, lead, and develop a global team of principal and senior principal engineers and technical specialists; create a pipeline of future-factory talent.
* **External engagement:** Develop strategic relationships with equipment OEMs, automation integrators, technology startups, academia, and industry bodies (e.g., ISPE) to benchmark and access emerging capabilities.
* **Executive communication:** Represent Factory of the Future in executive and enterprise forums, translating technical concepts into business outcomes.

 
**Qualifications** 

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering (Chemical, Mechanical, Biomedical, Electrical, Automation, Industrial, or related) required; Master’s, PhD, or MBA preferred.
* Minimum of 18 years of experience in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or medical device manufacturing, engineering, or technology, including 8+ years leading teams and large capital or technology programs.
* Proven record of leading greenfield/brownfield facility design or major site transformations from concept through startup.
* Expertise in aseptic and sterile manufacturing and/or biologics; experience across packaging, device, or chemical production is highly desirable.
* Demonstrated leadership in deploying Industry 4.0/5.0 technologies (robotics, automation, MES/MOM, IIoT, digital twins, AI/ML) at scale in GMP environments.
* Strong command of cGMP, Annex 1, data integrity, computer system assurance, and OT/IT cybersecurity expectations.
* Ability to build business cases and manage multi-million-dollar budgets and portfolios.
* Executive presence and ability to influence senior leaders across a global matrix organization.
* Experience developing and leading high-performing technical teams, including senior technical talent.
* Professional certifications (PE, PMP, ISPE CPIP) and a record of external publications, patents, or industry leadership are a plus.

 
**Additional Information**

Applicable only to applicants applying to a position in any location with pay disclosure requirements under state or local law:

* The compensation range described below is the range of possible base pay compensation that the Company believes in good faith it will pay for this role at the time of this posting based on the job grade for this position. Individual compensation paid within this range will depend on many factors including geographic location, and we may ultimately pay more or less than the posted range. This range may be modified in the future.
* We offer a comprehensive package of benefits including paid time off (vacation, holidays, sick), medical/dental/vision insurance and 401(k) to eligible employees.
* This job is eligible to participate in our long-term incentive programs.

Note: No amount of pay is considered to be wages or compensation until such amount is earned, vested, and determinable. The amount and availability of any bonus, commission, incentive, benefits, or any other form of compensation and benefits that are allocable to a particular employee remains in the Company's sole and absolute discretion unless and until paid and may be modified at the Company’s sole and absolute discretion, consistent with applicable law.

AbbVie is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to operating with integrity, driving innovation, transforming lives and serving our community. Equal Opportunity Employer/Veterans/Disabled.

US & Puerto Rico only - to learn more, visit https://www.abbvie.com/join-us/equal-employment-opportunity-employer.html

US & Puerto Rico applicants seeking a reasonable accommodation, click here to learn more:

https://www.abbvie.com/join-us/reasonable-accommodations.html

new_roles.title: Director of Operations
new_roles.description:
Karman Space & Defense is a leader in the rapid design, development, and production of critical, next-generation system solutions that align with the U.S. Department of War and its allies' core mission priorities, and meet the accelerating demand for access to space. Building on nearly 50 years of success, we deliver Payload & Protection Systems, Aero/Hydrodynamic Interstage Systems, and Propulsion & Launch Systems to more than 80 prime contractors supporting over 130 space and defense programs.

This role is part of our Space and Launch business, which has contributed to the nation's space programs for decades by delivering complete solutions from concept to flight. We enable successful space operations with mission-critical technology supporting every step from first launch to final landing, including launch vehicle subsystems, propulsion systems, aerodynamic and interstage systems, and payload protection and deployment. Our high-performance solutions are engineered to operate in the most extreme environments and meet precise mission requirements.

Lead manufacturing operations across Karman's El Monte and Corona locations, aligning machining, fabrication, and downstream processing with business objectives. In this role, you will drive safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, and profitability by providing operational leadership, strengthening cross-functional collaboration, and advancing continuous improvement initiatives across complex manufacturing environments.

**Responsibilities**

* Leads and coordinates manufacturing operations across the El Monte and Corona locations, establishing accountability, performance expectations, and operating rhythms for operations managers and functional departments.
* Develops and executes operational plans that align production performance, capacity, and investment priorities with company strategy.
* Oversees machining, fabrication, forming, finishing, and assembly operations to improve throughput, schedule attainment, labor productivity, and profitability.
* Drives operational excellence by implementing procedures and standards that improve safety, quality, delivery, cost, and regulatory compliance.
* Champions Lean manufacturing and continuous improvement through 5S, Kaizen, flow and lead-time improvements, cycle-time and setup reduction, Total Productive Maintenance (TPM), and preventative maintenance.
* Analyzes financial and production data, including overall equipment effectiveness (OEE), spindle utilization, and labor efficiency, to manage budgets, inventory, spending, and cost performance.
* Ensures equipment readiness, maintenance execution, and manufacturing capacity align with production requirements.
* Partners with human resources on workforce planning, recruiting, organizational structure, labor utilization, work scheduling, leadership development, performance evaluation, and succession planning.

new_roles.title: Director of Operations
new_roles.description:
**U C Coatings Director of Operations**

**Reports to** President

**Location** Based at a U-C Coatings facility; Buffalo, NY or Kenosha, WI preferred

**Travel** Approximately 25-35%, including regular travel to all four sites and 3PL partners

**Scope** Buffalo, Kenosha, Seattle and Portland manufacturing sites; 3PLs; supply chain and sourcing; customer service

**Position summary**

U-C Coatings manufactures specialty coatings, wood protection and repair products for industrial and consumer markets. The **Director of Operations** leads the people, processes and resources that turn customer demand into safe, reliable production and accurate, timely delivery.

Reporting to the President, this leader is accountable for operating performance across four sites and the supporting supply chain, sourcing, logistics and customer service functions. The role requires regular time on the production floor, strong financial judgment, and the ability to develop capable site and functional leaders in a lean organization.

**Manufacturing and site leadership**

* Lead site leaders in Buffalo, NY, Kenosha, WI, Seattle, WA, and Portland, OR; establish clear responsibilities, operating standards and performance expectations across the network.
* Translate demand into production, staffing and capacity plans; improve batch scheduling, filling, packaging, labor productivity and equipment utilization.
* Improve yield, reduce scrap and rework, and address recurring downtime through preventive maintenance, root cause analysis and practical process improvements.
* Evaluate production allocation, interplant transfers, capital investments and facility changes to improve service, cost and available capacity.

**Supply chain and sourcing**

* Own procurement and supplier performance for raw materials, packaging, purchased products and operating supplies; negotiate pricing, terms and service commitments.
* Lead monthly demand and supply planning with Sales and Finance; align forecasts, purchasing and production with service goals and working capital requirements.
* Set replenishment and inventory policies by item and site; improve inventory accuracy, reduce excess and obsolete stock, and prevent material shortages.
* Develop qualified alternate sources and continuity plans for critical inputs; coordinate supplier and material changes with Technical and Quality before implementation.

**Logistics and third party warehousing**

* Manage 3PL contracts, service standards and performance reviews, including inventory reconciliation, order accuracy, shipping performance, claims and invoice audits.
* Control inbound, outbound, parcel, LTL and interplant freight costs; improve packaging, carrier selection and routing while meeting customer requirements.

**Customer Service**

* Lead Customer Service from order receipt through fulfillment; improve order entry accuracy, acknowledgments, delivery commitments and response times.
* Connect Customer Service, Sales, planning, plants and 3PLs so customers receive reliable commitments and proactive updates on shortages or delays.
* Resolve escalated service issues, returns and credits with Sales, Finance and Technical; use complaint and shipping error trends to eliminate repeat failures.

**Safety quality and compliance**

* Hold site leaders accountable for safe operations, training, inspections, incident reporting and timely corrective action; maintain clear escalation and stop-work authority.
* Partner with internal specialists and outside advisers to meet applicable workplace safety, environmental, storage, waste and shipping requirements at each site.
* Ensure operating teams follow approved formulations, batch records, quality checks, labeling and lot traceability; support product launches and process changes with Technical and Quality.

**Financial management and people leadership**

* Own operating budgets and explain labor, material, freight and overhead variances with Finance; deliver verified savings and capital projects with clear returns.
* Coach and evaluate site and functional leaders; build staffing, cross-training and succession plans, and address performance issues promptly with HR support.
* Run weekly site and consolidated scorecard reviews covering service, cost, quality, inventory and people; assign owners and deadlines and verify corrective actions.

**Qualifications**

* Ten or more years of progressive manufacturing operations experience, including at least five years leading managers or major operating functions.
* Demonstrated success leading multiple manufacturing sites or a comparably complex manufacturing and distribution network; ability to lead dispersed teams.
* Practical experience with procurement, inventory planning, logistics, outsourced warehousing and customer fulfillment; strong cost and financial analysis skills.
* Experience with ERP and MRP systems, Excel, operating scorecards and continuous improvement; ability to turn data into decisions and sustained results.
* Bachelor's degree in operations, supply chain, engineering, business or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience. Coatings, chemicals, adhesives, sealants or other batch manufacturing experience is strongly preferred.

**Measures of success**

Accountable measures include safety controls; on-time, in-full delivery; labor efficiency; yield and cost of poor quality; inventory accuracy and turns; supplier and 3PL performance; freight costs; order accuracy; and leadership development. Agree on targets with the CEO after validating baselines.

**Initial priorities and working environment**

Within 90 days, assess the sites and key partners, validate scorecards, and agree on an improvement plan with owners, deadlines and financial impact. Work includes office, plant and warehouse activities, required PPE (company-provided), regular travel and occasional support outside business hours. Essential duties may be performed with reasonable accommodation.

**COMPANY DESCRIPTION:**

U-C Coatings is a leading manufacturer and supplier of premium wood protection products. For more than 50 years, our products have been used in a variety of industries, including hardwood and softwood logging and lumber production, wood products, manufacturing, woodworking, and wood decking markets.

Our products are used worldwide to protect, conserve, and enhance forest resources. Our goal is to help our customers achieve more with less waste and provide the highest level of protection for their products.

**ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:**

This role is an in-person role located within the company’s Kenosha, WI location. There is a moderate noise level within the work environment. Compliance with applicable Company policies including maintaining a drug-free workplace and adhering to all safety policies and procedures is required.

**DISCLAIMERS:**

UC Coatings, LLC reserves the right to revise, change or modify the duties and responsibilities of this position at any time to meet business needs. This job description may not list all duties for this position. This job description is not a contract of employment, and all UC Coatings, LLC employment unless otherwise disclosed is “at will” and either the incumbent or UC Coatings, LLC may terminate employment at any time for any reason.

UC Coatings, LLC is an Equal opportunity, inclusive employer and will consider all applicants for employment with the Company based on merit, competence, and qualifications without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, sexual orientation, or any other category protected by federal, state, or local law.

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Employee assistance program
* Flexible spending account
* Health insurance
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Vision insurance

Education:

* Bachelor's (Required)

Experience:

* Operations management: 5 years (Required)

Willingness to travel:

* 50% (Preferred)

Work Location: In person

new_roles.title: Contract Manufacturing Director
new_roles.description:
**Lassonde Pappas & Co.** is a US Leader in beverage manufacturing dedicated to our team members, customers and consumers satisfaction. We remain committed to our small-town roots and rural values. **Hardworking** and **caring** are qualities that make our teams special. Since 1942, we’ve been producing delicious products for our customers across the country!

To provide the best for our customers, we focus on building the best team by creating and advancing an inclusive environment amongst our diverse workforces. If you’re passionate about customer satisfaction, reliable, and committed to being and doing better, join us!

**We value each of our employees’ total wellbeing. To support employees in all stages of their wellness journey, we have a robust benefits program including medical, dental, and vision coverage options, growth and development potential, along with 401-K, Life & Disability Insurance, PTO, Tuition Reimbursement, Health Fairs, Gym Membership Discounts, and so much more!**

*Pay Range for this position is: $165,000-$200,000 plus annual bonus, depending on experience and geographical location.*

**POSITION SUMMARY**

The **Director, Contract Manufacturing** reports to the Vice President, Integrated Planning, U.S. Beverage and is based in Cherry Hill, New Jersey.

The Director is responsible for defining the role of contract manufacturing within the Beverage Division’s broader supply network and translating business plans into clear external capacity, capability, geographic, and partnership requirements across the U.S. and Canada. This role leads the development and optimization of the contract manufacturing network to ensure the right capabilities, capacity, cost, quality, service, and resilience to support business growth.

The Director oversees relationships with contract manufacturing partners from initial capability assessment and commercial selection through operational integration, product launch, ongoing governance, and continuous performance improvement.

The Director aligns internal business and functional leaders around external manufacturing decisions and builds productive relationships with strategic partners. The role ensures that external manufacturing resources are positioned to support the division’s growth plans, innovation agenda, service expectations, cost objectives, and business continuity requirements.

**Up to 25% travel required**

**RESPONSIBILITIES**

**External Manufacturing Strategy & Network Optimization**

* Define and execute the contract manufacturing strategy for the Beverage Division across the U.S. and Canada, translating business requirements into external manufacturing capacity, capability, geographic, and partnership needs.
* Optimize the existing contract manufacturing network by assessing manufacturing capabilities, capacity, geographic footprint, technology, cost, service, quality, and supply risk.
* Partner with Integrated Planning, Operations, Finance, Procurement, and other key stakeholders on make-versus-buy decisions and long-term capacity strategies.
* Maintain a strong understanding of the external manufacturing landscape to identify new capabilities, technologies, potential partners, and opportunities to strengthen the overall supply network.

**Strategic Sourcing & Commercial Management**

* Translate business requirements into sourcing strategies for externally manufactured products, balancing economics, available capacity, technical capability, speed, flexibility, and supply risk.
* Lead competitive sourcing and partner-selection activities, including market assessment, RFIs/RFPs/RFQs, commercial evaluation, supplier selection, negotiation, contracting, and implementation.
* Structure and negotiate commercial agreements that clearly define pricing, capacity commitments, service expectations, quality requirements, flexibility provisions, liability, and business continuity obligations.
* Develop fact-based sourcing recommendations considering total cost of ownership, capacity, capability, risk, and overall strategic fit.
* Establish pricing mechanisms and commercial frameworks that promote transparency, competitiveness, and sustainable productivity.
* Provide financial stewardship of external manufacturing spend through disciplined budgeting, forecasting, cost analysis, variance management, and productivity delivery.

**Supplier Relationship & Performance Management**

* Establish and lead a structured Supplier Relationship Management (SRM) approach for strategic contract manufacturing partners.
* Establish and maintain a robust performance management framework and supplier scorecards for the contract manufacturing network.
* Establish a disciplined operating rhythm with strategic partners, supported by agreed performance measures, periodic operating and executive business reviews, documented recovery plans, and clear ownership of actions.
* Build strategic relationships with key external manufacturing partners to improve service, strengthen capacity and flexibility, accelerate innovation, and identify productivity opportunities.
* Lead supplier and network risk assessments and ensure appropriate business continuity, contingency, and risk mitigation plans are developed and maintained.

The Director owns the performance framework for the external manufacturing network, ensuring that targets reflect the division’s priorities for customer service, product quality, delivered cost, productivity, available capacity, launch execution, contractual compliance, and supply continuity. The role is responsible for converting performance information into timely decisions, recovery actions, and clear visibility of results and risks for business leadership.

**Commercialization & Cross-Functional Execution**

* Lead the external manufacturing workstream for new product commercialization, capacity expansions, product transfers, and new contract manufacturer onboarding.
* Partner with R&D, Marketing, Quality, Engineering, Operations, Integrated Planning, and other key functions to ensure new products and external manufacturing capabilities are launched on time, at target cost, and in accordance with quality and regulatory requirements.
* Ensure effective integration of contract manufacturers into the broader planning and supply network, including capacity planning, production planning, inventory management, service, and supply continuity.
* Coordinate resolution of operational and supply issues across internal functions and external manufacturing partners, ensuring clear ownership and escalating material business risks when required.

**Team Leadership & Governance**

* Lead, coach, and develop the Contract Manufacturing team, establishing clear goals, accountability, and individual development plans.
* Establish the governance, processes, tools, decision rights, and performance standards required to effectively manage the external manufacturing network.
* Ensure accurate and actionable contract manufacturing information is maintained, including supplier capabilities, capacity, pricing, commercial terms, products/SKUs, performance, and contractual commitments.
* Provide business leadership with regular visibility into external manufacturing cost, capacity, service, performance, supply risk, and opportunities, enabling timely and informed decision-making.
* Drive cross-functional alignment and accountability for initiatives and decisions affecting the external manufacturing network.

**EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE**

**Minimum Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Engineering, Operations Management, Business Administration, or a related field.
* 10+ years of progressive experience in contract manufacturing, external manufacturing, strategic sourcing, procurement, operations, or supply chain, preferably within the CPG, food, or beverage industry.
* Demonstrated experience managing third-party manufacturing relationships and complex commercial agreements.
* Strong experience in strategic sourcing, supplier negotiations, contracting, and supplier relationship management.
* Experience leading complex cross-functional initiatives involving Operations, Planning, Quality, R&D, Finance, Procurement, and Commercial teams.
* Demonstrated ability to evaluate cost, capacity, capability, service, quality, and supply risk and translate analysis into effective business recommendations.
* Strong financial and analytical acumen, including experience with budgeting, forecasting, cost modeling, and productivity initiatives.
* Proven ability to influence senior stakeholders and external business partners within a complex matrix organization.
* Strong leadership, communication, negotiation, problem-solving, and change-management skills.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience in the food, beverage, or broader CPG industry.
* Experience managing a multi-site or North American external manufacturing network.
* Experience with new product commercialization, manufacturing transfers, and external partner onboarding.
* APICS/ASCM certification, CPSM, or comparable supply chain/procurement certification.
* MBA or advanced degree.

**SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Directly manages three employees, providing coaching, development, performance management, and clear accountability for results.
* Establishes team priorities, objectives, and performance expectations aligned with the contract manufacturing strategy and broader business goals.
* Builds team capability and expertise while fostering a culture of ownership, collaboration, continuous improvement, and results.
* Provides leadership across a broader cross-functional network, influencing internal stakeholders and external manufacturing partners to achieve service, quality, cost, capacity, innovation, and supply continuity objectives.
* Leads through influence across a matrix organization, driving alignment and accountability among internal functions and strategic external partners.

**PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS & WORKING CONDITIONS**

This position requires sufficient physical ability to work in a typical office setting; driving a motor vehicle, taking the plane, doing north American travel and occasionally working in the field.

**FREQUENT:** sitting, upward and downward flexion of neck; fine finger dexterity and light to moderate finger pressure to include extended periods of keyboard and mouse use, side-to-side turning of neck, walking, standing, bending and stooping, pushing/pulling, twisting at waist, moderate wrist torque to twist equipment knobs and dials.

**OCCASIONAL:** squatting, kneeling, reach above and at shoulder height, moderate grasp to manipulate reference books and manuals; lifting objects weighing 20 – 35 lbs. from below waist to above shoulders and transporting distances up to 50 feet.

**VISION:** Ability to see in the normal visual range with or without correction.

new_roles.title: Plant Manager - Dairy Preferred
new_roles.description:
**Confidential Search: ESL Processing Manager – Dairy Manufacturing** 
**Location:** Greater Philadelphia, PA Area 
**Industry:** Dairy / Food & Beverage Manufacturing 
**Employment Type:** Full-time, Onsite 
**Compensation:** Competitive Base + Bonus + Full Benefits 
**Confidential Role – Qualified candidates only will be contacted directly**

### **Position Summary**

A well-established dairy manufacturer in the Philadelphia region is conducting a confidential search for an experienced **ESL Processing Manager**. This role will oversee operations related to extended shelf life milk and dairy beverage processing, with a strong focus on product quality, plant performance, and regulatory compliance.

The ideal candidate will have direct experience with **HTST, UHT, or ESL pasteurization systems**, a deep understanding of **fluid dairy processing**, and a proven ability to lead production teams in a **fast-paced, SQF-certified environment**.

### **Key Responsibilities**

* Lead daily operations of the ESL processing department, ensuring product quality and production efficiency.
* Manage HTST/UHT equipment, CIP/SIP procedures, and aseptic processing protocols.
* Oversee batch formulation, temperature and flow controls, and compliance with state and federal regulations.
* Coordinate production schedules, sanitation cycles, and preventative maintenance in conjunction with QA and maintenance teams.
* Lead, train, and supervise ESL line operators and processing staff; enforce safety, GMP, and food safety practices.
* Monitor and improve KPIs related to yield, run efficiency, downtime, and loss.
* Collaborate with R&D, Quality Assurance, Packaging, and Distribution teams on process improvement initiatives.

### **Required Qualifications**

* 5+ years of dairy or beverage processing experience, with at least 2 years in an ESL, HTST, or UHT operation.
* Strong understanding of fluid milk or dairy-based beverage production and regulatory compliance (FDA, PMO).
* Supervisory or leadership experience in a food manufacturing plant.
* Familiarity with CIP/SIP systems, flow schematics, and thermal processing validation.
* Bachelor’s degree in Food Science, Dairy Science, Engineering, or a related field preferred.
* Strong communication, problem-solving, and organizational skills.
* Experience working in SQF-certified or similar food safety environments.

### **Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience with aseptic packaging lines or ESL bottled products.
* Pasteurizer or processing certifications (e.g., HACCP, SQF Practitioner).
* Knowledge of automation systems (e.g., PLCs, SCADA) used in fluid processing.

**To Apply Confidentially:** 
Please send your resume and brief cover note to **laws@henpencorp.com** 
Or text **408-755-5423** to express interest.

*Only qualified applicants with relevant dairy or ESL processing experience will be contacte*

new_roles.title: Plant Manager
new_roles.description:
Location:
Niles, IL, US, 60714

Req ID: 41695

Segment: Operations

Rich’s, also known as Rich Products Corporation, is a family-owned food company dedicated to inspiring possibilities. From cakes and icings to pizza, appetizers and specialty toppings, our products are used in homes, restaurants and bakeries around the world. Beyond great food, our customers also gain insights to help them stay competitive, no matter their size. Our portfolio includes creative solutions geared at helping food industry professionals compete in foodservice, retail, in-store bakery, deli, and prepared foods, among others. With more than 13,500 associates working globally in 100 countries and annual sales of $5.9 billion, Rich’s is a global leader with a focus on everything that family makes possible. Rich’s®—Infinite Possibilities. One Family.

**Purpose Statement**
---------------------

The Plant Manager's responsibility is to provide leadership to all departments for overall vision and direction of the plant by way of guidance, direction, encouragement, training and development. Also developing and coaching managers and supervisors to excel to the peak of their performance levels. In addition to directing all managerial personnel to manage their departments and functional areas to meet the manufacturing plant’s operational and financial objectives while supporting the values, mission, vision, and priorities of Rich Products Corporation.

**Key Accountabilities and Outcomes**
-------------------------------------

new_roles.title: Rendering Plant Manager
new_roles.description:
UniSea is looking for an experienced Rendering Plant Manager to lead and manage operations of UniSea’s fish rendering plant in Dutch Harbor, Alaska. The Rendering Plant Manager will be working at our Dutch Harbor, Alaska operations.

The Rendering Plant Manager is responsible for managing all elements of production of Fish Meal, Bone Meal, Fish Oil, and other by-products at UniSea’s Meal Plant to achieve continuous operations and maximum profitability. Maintain efficient operations of Main Sump operation in compliance with all State and Federal requirements.

**Essential Duties**

1) Organize and manage production staff and manage activities of the Meal Plant processing operation and maintain operational performance of equipment in the Main Sump. Coordinate production based on G1 and G2 operations.

2) Work with the Maintenance department in proposing and making design changes in processing facilities and equipment to maximize plant efficiency. Submit work orders to maintain proper repair of processing facility on repair or installation work that the Meal Plant does not perform.

3) Counsel and train employees according to UniSea policies and procedures. Coach and motivate employees to achieve maximum performance and maintain high morale. Evaluate employee performance and take necessary steps to assist employees in improving performance. Administer discipline to employees as appropriate, including terminations.

4) Recommend capital equipment needs, methods of improvement, and tools and materials to maintain and improve competitive production efficiency.

5) Maintain knowledge about internal and external influences affecting the future of the industry and company.

6) Review and assure the accuracy of scale reports, production reports, shipping tallies, inventories and quality control reports.

7) Coordinate with machinery manufacturers in updating current technology as appropriate.

8) Assist safety personnel and promote good safety and hygiene procedures throughout the plant.

9) Maintain open communication with the Quality Assurance department to ensure product specification, micro, and labeling requirements are maintained.

10) Perform other duties as directed.

**Position Requirements**

· High School or equivalent is required.

· Vocational education in a skilled trade like Electrical, Plumbing, HVAC, or Welding is preferred.

· Must have a minimum of 6 years of experience working in a rendering plant.

· Must have 2 years of experience in managing and supervising employees.

· Must have excellent leadership, communication and interpersonal skills.

· Must be able and willing to work in a rendering plant and supervise employees’ work performance in the plant.

· Working proficiency with Microsoft Outlook, Excel and Teams.

· Must be able to pass a post offer drug screen and criminal background check.

**This is a salaried exempt position located in Dutch Harbor, Alaska with a starting salary within the range of $96,754 - $116,122 per year.**

UniSea offers a rich benefits package including:

- Free company provided housing and utilities for employees in Dutch Harbor, Alaska.

- Free meals for employees in the company galley. Discounted meals are available for family members living in Alaska.

- Annual travel allowance benefit

- Relocation assistance

- Medical/Dental/Vision insurance available after 60-day eligibility period is satisfied

- A variety of different voluntary coverages are offered – including AFLAC policies and additional life insurance for self and family members

- Flexible Spending Account (FSA) and Dependent Care Accounts are available after 60-day eligibility period is satisfied

- 401(k) plan and additional 3% employer contribution – after 6-month eligibility period is satisfied. UniSea matches 100% of your contributions up to the first 5%, plus makes an additional 3% employer contribution.

- Employer paid life insurance

- Paid vacation, sick leave, and holidays

UniSea is an Equal Employment Opportunity employer.

Pay: $96,754.00 - $116,122.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Employee assistance program
* Flexible spending account
* Health insurance
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Professional development assistance
* Relocation assistance
* Retirement plan
* Vision insurance

People with a criminal record are encouraged to apply

Experience:

* rendering plant: 6 years (Required)
* Supervising: 2 years (Required)

Ability to Relocate:

* Dutch Harbor, AK 99692: Relocate with an employer provided relocation package (Required)

Work Location: In person

new_roles.title: Plant Manager
new_roles.description:
Linde Advanced Material Technologies Inc.

**Plant Manager**

Ellisville, MS, United States | req34514

**What you will enjoy doing\***

* Lead the Ellisville manufacturing operation with full accountability for Safety, Quality, Delivery, and Cost (SQDC), while ensuring customer commitments and business objectives are consistently achieved
* Build and develop a high-performing leadership team by setting clear expectations, coaching managers and supervisors, strengthening accountability, and developing organizational capability and succession
* You will drive the PGT Lean Operating System through daily management, leader standard work, visual management, structured problem solving, standard work, and continuous improvement
* Be a visible leader on the shop floor, working with teams at the source to identify problems, remove barriers, strengthen process discipline, and ensure corrective actions address root causes and are sustained
* Improve operational performance and reliability by strengthening equipment performance, first-pass yield, flow, WIP, productivity, capacity, and on-time delivery while maintaining uncompromising safety and quality standards
* Develop and execute the site strategy, aligning workforce, training, equipment, materials, capital, and capacity with customer demand, growth priorities, and long-term business requirements
* Own the financial performance of the facility, including budgets, labor efficiency, overtime, productivity, cost improvement, operational spending, and capital priorities
* Also, you will lead cross-functionally and create a strong site culture, partnering with Operations, Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, Maintenance, EHS, Human Resources, and Finance while fostering respect, transparency, employee engagement, urgency, and continuous improvement

**What makes you great**

* You have a Bachelor’s degree with ten (10) or more years of related manufacturing experience, a Master’s degree with eight (8) or more years, a PhD with five (5) or more years, or sixteen (16) or more years of directly related manufacturing experience
* Further you have significant manufacturing leadership experience with accountability for safety, quality, delivery, cost, people, and operational results
* You have successfully led leaders, including managers and frontline supervisors, and know how to build capability rather than becoming the organization’s primary problem solver
* You have demonstrated experience applying Lean principles, daily management, standard work, and structured problem solving to deliver measurable operational improvement
* And you bring strong financial and business acumen, with experience managing budgets, labor, productivity, operating costs, and capital priorities
* Experience in aerospace, coatings, special processes, precision manufacturing, or another highly regulated manufacturing environment is strongly preferred
* You are comfortable leading change in a complex manufacturing environment and can move effectively between strategy, data, the shop floor, and customer and business priorities
* Most importantly, you lead with humility, accountability, transparency, respect for people, and a bias for action, while developing others and creating sustainable systems for success

**Why you will love working with us**

Linde is a leading global industrial gases and engineering company with 2025 sales of $34 billion. We live our mission of making our world more productive every day by providing high-quality solutions, technologies and services which are making our customers more successful and helping to sustain, decarbonize and protect our planet.
 
 
Linde serves a variety of end markets such as chemicals & energy, food & beverage, electronics, healthcare, manufacturing, metals and mining. Linde’s industrial gases and technologies are used in countless applications, enabling space exploration and launch technologies, delivering ultra-high-purity and specialty gases for semiconductor manufacturing, providing life-saving medical oxygen and enabling clean hydrogen production and carbon capture to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. Linde also delivers state-of-the-art gas processing solutions to support customer growth, efficiency improvements and emissions reductions.

**What we offer you!**

At Linde, the sky is not the limit. If you’re looking to build a career where your work reaches beyond your job description and betters the people with whom you work, the communities we serve, and the world in which we all live, at Linde, your opportunities are limitless. Be Linde. Be Limitless. 
 
Linde offers competitive compensation and an outstanding benefits package. Enjoy access to health, dental, disability, and life insurance, paid holidays and vacation, 401(k) matching, pension benefits, an employee discount program, and opportunities for educational and professional growth. Additional compensation may vary depending on the position and organizational level. Build your future with us while making an impact every day!

**Have we inspired you? Let´s talk about it**

We are looking forward to receiving your complete application.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, protected veteran status, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other reason prohibited by applicable law. 
 
Linde Advanced Material Technologies Inc. abides by applicable export control laws including the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) in accordance with the company's export control procedures. As such, persons considered for this position must be either a U.S. Citizen, Permanent Resident (green card holder) or otherwise classifiable as a U.S. person under relevant regulations. 
 
Linde Advanced Material Technologies Inc. acts responsibly towards its shareholders, business partners, employees, society and the environment in every one of its business areas, regions and locations across the globe. The company is committed to technologies and products that unite the goals of customer value and sustainable development. 
 

* The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by employees assigned to this classification. They are not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties and skills required of employees assigned to this position. Therefore employees assigned may be required to perform additional job tasks required by the manager.

new_roles.title: Plant Manager
new_roles.description:
**Position Summary**

We are seeking a team-oriented, hands-on Plant Manager with a robust background in maintenance leadership. This role is responsible for overseeing all aspects of plant operations, with a particular emphasis on developing and executing a world-class maintenance program at our mill in St. Maries, Idaho. The ideal candidate will drive operational excellence, safety, and continuous improvement, ensuring the facility meets production goals while maintaining the highest standards of equipment reliability and team development.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead the plant’s manufacturing and maintenance operations, ensuring safe, efficient, and reliable production.
* Oversee preventive, predictive, and proactive maintenance programs, including planning, scheduling, and execution.
* Direct and develop a multidisciplinary team, including Maintenance Planners, Millwrights, Electricians, Mechanics, and Production Supervisors.
* Foster a “Safety First” culture, ensuring compliance with all safety and environmental regulations and serving as a role model for safe industrial behavior.
* Collaborate with other departments (Finance, HR, Sales, Marketing, Resources) to align plant performance with company goals and market demands.
* Drive continuous improvement initiatives, leveraging best practices in manufacturing and maintenance to optimize resources and processes.
* Lead and support improvement projects, including research, cost analysis, financial justification, and project management from conception to completion.
* Manage key performance indicators for maintenance and production, such as safety compliance, PM completion, downtime, overtime, expense controls, and plant cleanliness.
* Develop and retain high-performing teams through effective communication, training, and empowerment.
* Build strong relationships across the organization, ensuring active communication and teamwork.
* Utilize modern maintenance management tools (e.g., CMMS, AutoCAD, MS Suite) and interpret technical documents (e.g., blueprints).

**Qualifications**

* Proven experience in plant management or senior manufacturing leadership, with a strong track record in maintenance supervision and program development.
* Minimum of five years in maintenance leadership, with hands-on experience in preventive, predictive, and proactive maintenance.
* Strong technical skills in troubleshooting mechanical, electrical, hydraulic, pneumatic, and strong understanding of PLC systems.
* Demonstrated ability to lead, motivate, and develop teams in a continuous improvement environment.
* Excellent analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
* Effective communicator, able to set clear expectations and drive accountability.
* Experience with process optimization.
* Business acumen to manage budgets, control costs, and justify investments.
* High school diploma required; college-level education in a related field preferred.

new_roles.title: Plant Manager
new_roles.description:
**Pacific Coast Producers |** Full-Time | On-Site | Exempt 
**Salary Range:** $160,000- $200,000 /year (based on experience)

**Pacific Coast Producers** (PCP), a growing agricultural cooperative with food production facilities across the West Coast, is seeking an experienced and strategic **Plant Manager** to lead our Production Facility **in Lodi, CA**. PCP is dedicated to investing in its people and fostering a culture of service, where each employee can do their best to make affordable, high-quality food for customers across North America.

Join our legacy of talented people working together to innovate and lead our industry. As a member of PCP, you will have access to a comprehensive benefits package that includes top-quality, medical, dental, and vision insurance, generous paid time off, and a retirement savings plan to help secure your future.

The Plant Manager will have overall accountability for directing and managing plant operations to meet quality, food safety, and customer requirements in a safe, cost-effective, and timely manner. The plant employs over 800 employees during the processing season and maintains an experienced year-round staff. The Plant Manager reports directly to the Director of Operations.

**What You'll Do:**

* Lead all aspects of plant operations, ensuring safe, efficient, and high-quality production
* Develop and execute production plans aligned with raw material supply, demand, labor, and plant capacity
* Drive performance against key metrics including safety, quality, throughput, and cost
* Own operating and capital budgets; analyzing performance and implementing corrective actions
* Champion food safety, environmental compliance, and regulatory adherence (OSHA, FDA, SQF, HACCP, HARPC, GMPs)
* Build, coach, and develop strong teams through clear expectations and consistent leadership
* Lead continuous improvement initiatives to enhance efficiency, reliability, and profitability
* Partner effectively with union leadership to maintain a positive and productive work environment
* Oversee capital projects and internal investments to support future growth and operational excellence

**What You Bring to the Team:**

* 10+ years of progressive leadership experience in food manufacturing including aseptic processing, canning, or similar method.
* Bachelor’s degree in Business, Engineering, or related field
* Proven ability to lead large teams in a fast-paced, unionized setting
* Proven experience with process flows, automated controls, review of AutoCAD drawings, and dealing with industrial processing equipment vendors and mechanical contractors.
* Strong operational and financial acumen, including budgeting and performance analysis
* Demonstrated success driving continuous improvement and leading change
* Deep understanding of food safety systems and regulatory requirements (GFSI, HACCP, HARPC, FDA, OSHA)
* Hands-on leadership style with strong problem-solving capability
* Ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver results under tight timelines
* Strong communication skills with the ability to influence across all levels of the organization

**Why Join PCP?**

At PCP, we take care of our people. Here are just a few of the benefits full-time employees enjoy:

* **Competitive pay** with opportunities for advancement.
* **This position is eligible for our annual profit-sharing bonus program**.
* **Medical, dental, and vision coverage for you and your family, starting the first of the month after you join us.**
* **Retirement plans** to support your long-term security.
* **Paid time off** including vacation, holidays, parental leave, sick leave, and bereavement.
* **Life and disability insurance** plus an Employee Assistance Program.
* **Development opportunities** through online courses, classroom training, and on-the-job growth.
* The stability of a **farmer-owned cooperative** with more than 50 years of success.
* A mission-driven culture focused on **feeding families across North America.**

**Salary Range: $160,000 - $200,000/year (based on experience).** This is a **full-time, on-site** role based at our production facility Lodi, CA.

The base salary range reflects the reasonable expectation for what the company anticipates paying for this role at the time of posting. The actual salary offered will depend on factors including, but not limited to:

* Relevant skills, education, and experience
* Job-related qualifications and certifications
* Internal pay equity
* Market conditions and business needs

**Sponsorship:** This role is not eligible for current or future visa sponsorship.

**About PCP Summary**

Founded in 1971, Pacific Coast Producers is owned by more than 165 family farmers who cultivate and deliver a diverse range of crops including tomatoes, peaches, pears, grapes, cherries, and more. Our cooperative operates multiple processing and packaging facilities across the West Coast, supplying top-quality products to grocery retailers and foodservice distributors throughout the U.S. and Canada.

Our Lodi Production facility is a bustling hub where delicious apples, peaches, and apricots are transformed into high-quality products. The facility is equipped with advanced machinery and cutting-edge technology, enabling efficient and precise sorting, peeling, and slicing of the fruits. Meticulous attention is paid to every step of the process, ensuring that only the finest fruits make their way into the final products.

Nestled in the heart of San Joaquin County and just a short 45-minute drive from Sacramento, our Production Facility is located in the charming city of Lodi, CA. Lodi is renowned for its rich history in winemaking and agriculture, as well as its vibrant downtown area and close-knit community. With a great quality of life, Lodi offers a welcoming environment to those seeking a relaxed and enjoyable lifestyle.

**AA/EEO Policy Statement**

Pacific Coast Producers is an affirmative action and equal opportunity employer. No employee or applicant will be discriminated against in any condition of employment because of race, color, national origin, sex, religion, age, disability, veteran status, or any other status protected by law.

new_roles.title: Director, Site Operations
new_roles.description:
**The Role**
------------

The Director, Site Operations leads all aspects of our plant operations ranging from the cultivation of cannabis through distribution and everything in between. As the Director, Site Operations, you'll direct all the daily processes and long-term targets for the facility. You'll grind away at the details of managing internal resources to maximize safety, compliance, efficiency, productivity and culture. You'll also blaze the path toward creating and developing the multilevel professional team, and you'll work closely with your management team to keep every detail of the facility up to standards.

**Essential Functions**
-----------------------

* Oversee all strategic planning and vision for facility plant operations for cultivation, processing, packaging, maintenance, quality and logistics/fulfillment
* Manager all facility activities working closely with departmental managers ensuring wholesale objectives are accomplished on time and budget
* Own the facility budget; Analyze facility data, including efficiency metrics, labor variance analysis, defect rates, cost drivers, volume and capacity planning, etc. to make recommendations on optimal quality and efficiency improvements and capital expenditures
* Develop and produce reporting to clearly illustrate the trends of the business
* Manage and maintain a company culture consistent with the culture established at Green Thumb corporate of accountability, transparency and enjoyment
* Participate in developing and implementing rules, regulations, policies, and procedures to advance Green Thumb's mission, vision, goals and objectives
* Continuously improve the skills, knowledge and morale of all employees; create an environment where the entire team does the same
* Implement and maintain wholesale facility and equipment preventative maintenance program; replace, or make adjustments to plant facilities and equipment when necessary
* Ensure compliance with local, state, and federal billing or licensing requirements
* Will be required to be on-call and to respond to emergency situations at any time. This may include scheduling issues, potentially covering a vacant shift, facility issues and/or human resources requirements
* Other duties as assigned

**Safety & Compliance**
-----------------------

* Be aware of hazards in the workspace.
* Retain and understand department specific training.
* Be compliant with area safety requirements, state regulations and PPE requirements while at GTI sites.
* Follow GMP, biosecurity, sanitation or other quality and compliance requirements.
* Perform record keeping accurately and completely as directed by a lead or supervisor.
* Report and escalate safety & quality concerns.

**Working Conditions**
----------------------

* While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to perform reaching, grasping, bending, stooping, talking, hearing, seeing and repetitive motions.
* Ability to work in a fast-paced, changing, and challenging environment
* Work involves daily exposure to allergens (such as cannabis, tree nuts, and coconut oil).
* Travel up to 10% may be required

**Qualifications**
------------------

* Bachelor's Degree in Engineering or Business required; MBA or similar preferred
* 10+ years of management experience in manufacturing environment; direct management of 100+ individuals in a manufacturing setting required
* Consumer Packaged Good experience required
* In-depth knowledge & understanding of Lean, Six Sigma, certifications a plus
* Exposure to horticulture and/or plant science and/or lab processing, a plus
* Strong commercial and financial acumen with experience managing a P&L required
* Can-do attitude and ability to adapt quickly; business is experiencing tremendous growth so previous operational experience in growth environment is substantially preferred
* Highly motivated, self-directed, innovative and able to work independently or among teams with keen judgement, common sense and resourcefulness
* Adapts and thrives in a demanding, fast-paced environment
* Possesses a high level of critical thinking
* Operates with a high level of professionalism and integrity, including dealing with confidential information
* Must understand and comply with the rules, regulations, policies, and procedures of Green Thumb
* Must have a solid understanding of the Cannabis laws, rules and regulations and passion to further their understanding and knowledge of the industry and the laws.

**Additional Requirements**
---------------------------

* Must be at a minimum of 21 years of age.
* Must possess valid state ID.
* Must be able to obtain, and maintain, state badging requirements to work in the cannabis industry (requires background check and state review)
