new_roles.title: Director of Operations
new_roles.description:
**Overview**

The Operations Director will play a critical leadership role in the transformation and growth of Sterling Pharmaceutical Services. This individual must be a results-driven leader capable of accelerating operational excellence, strengthening organizational accountability, and improving financial performance while maintaining the highest standards of quality, compliance, and safety. The successful candidate will possess a strong sense of urgency, a hands-on leadership style, and a demonstrated track record of leading operational improvements, driving profitability, and delivering measurable results during periods of significant change and growth. The Operations Director will partner closely with executive leadership and regularly communicate progress, strategy, and performance metrics to key stakeholders, including ownership and the Board of Directors.

**Responsibilities**

* Lead operational and organizational initiatives to improve profitability, cash flow, productivity, and customer satisfaction.
* Develop and execute strategic plans that align operational performance with company financial objectives.
* Establish a culture of accountability, urgency, continuous improvement, and measurable results.
* Identify, prioritize, and implement operational efficiencies that reduce costs and improve margins.
* Drive cross-functional execution against key business objectives and recovery plans.
* Monitor and report operational metrics to executive leadership and the Board of Directors.
* Prepare and deliver presentations to executive leadership, Board members, lenders, investors, and external stakeholders.
* Partner closely with the CEO and COO to develop operational strategies and communicate progress against strategic initiatives.
* Lead change management efforts and effectively manage resistance during transformation initiatives.
* Ensure rapid decision-making and execution while maintaining compliance, quality, and safety standards.

**Requirements**

* B.S. in Engineering or Science discipline
* 10+ years of Operations Leadership experience. GMP aseptic manufacturing experience a plus.
* Demonstrated experience leading business transformation, operational turnarounds, restructurings, or significant performance improvement initiatives.
* Strong financial acumen with experience managing budgets, forecasting, cost reduction programs, EBITDA improvement, and working capital initiatives.
* Experience presenting to Boards of Directors, private equity firms, investors, lenders, or ownership groups.
* Track record of building high-performing teams and holding leaders accountable to performance metrics.
* Exceptional executive communication and presentation skills.

**Additional Information**

* Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States. Sterling Pharmaceutical Services does not sponsor employment visas now or in the future for this position.
* Relocation assistance is not available for this role. Candidates should reside within a reasonable commuting distance of the facility or be willing to relocate at their own expense.
* Sterling Pharmaceutical Services is conducting this search directly and is not engaging external recruiting or search firms for this position. We respectfully request that agencies and recruiters refrain from contacting us regarding candidate submissions.

Pay: $140,000.00 - $180,000.00 per year

Benefits:

new_roles.title: Director of Operations - Aiken, SC
new_roles.description:
**Job Overview**
----------------

The Director of Operations is responsible for the activities of manufacturing, purchasing, quality, planning (supply chain), and project management of the organization and aids in formulating and administering organization policies.

#LI-SL1

**A Day In The Life**
---------------------

Every day at Hubbell is different and you’ll contribute in many ways. On any given day, you’ll make a difference by:

* Participating in formulating/administering company policies and developing long range goals/objectives.
* Directing/coordinating activities of the responsible departments on a day-to-day basis to ensure that daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, and annual objectives are met.
* Ensuring internal auditing for compliance with the ISO standards applicable.
* Driving cost reduction (productivity) planning and execution in accordance with the financial plan.
* Providing authorization for funds to ensure responsible fiduciary spending in accordance with financial policies.
* Reviewing/analyzing activities related to costs, operations, CAPEX, and forecast data to determine progress toward financial goals and objectives and considering the long-range impact of growing the business and adjusting actions to ensure compliance.
* Overseeing the budget/forecast processes as well as ongoing monitoring to ensure compliance.
* Conferring with other senior personnel to review achievements and discuss required changes in goals or objectives resulting from current status/conditions.
* Developing plans and executing actions to meet the decision upon actions.
* Providing oversight and coordination to other business in Operations related matters to drive consistency among the businesses.
* Participating in due diligence process as requested.
* Developing succession planning strategies in coordination with HR to ensure continuation of leadership/individual contributor roles going forward.

**What will help you thrive in this role?**
-------------------------------------------

* Bachelor’s Degree in Business Management, Industrial Engineering, or related field
* Master’s Degree in Business Administration (required)
* 20+ years of relevant operations experience (required)
* 20+ years of experience as a Senior Plant Manager, Operations Manager, or a similar role, preferably in a heavy manufacturing environment with multi-site responsibility
* 10+ years of experience with TPM and SAP
* Welding, Fabricating, Warehouse & Logistics experience
* Operational Excellence or Lean Certification
* Strong knowledge of Lean Manufacturing
* Staff development and engagement skills
* Bi-lingual Spanish/English preferred

**Hubbell Incorporated**

Hubbell creates critical infrastructure solutions that power our customers, communities, people and the planet. Our company is strategically aligned around enabling grid modernization and electrification. As more products plug in to an aging grid, Hubbell solutions enable the transition to a more reliable, resilient and efficient energy infrastructure. Founded in 1888 our innovation has made us a leading global manufacturer of high quality electrical and utility solutions enabling customers to operate critical infrastructure reliably and efficiently.

The company operates in two segments. Hubbell Utility Solutions (HUS) enable the grid to conduct, communicate and control energy across utility applications and Hubbell Electrical Solutions (HES) are essential to managing power across a wide range of industries and applications. Our vertical market solutions can be applied to markets including Data Centers, Renewables, Commercial Buildings, Industrial, Telecom and Transportation. Supporting both of our business segments is our corporate and Hubbell Unified Business Solutions teams that provide consistent process, tools technologies across our businesses.

We are committed to operating sustainably and ethically while promoting an inclusive and supportive culture for our people to grow and develop in their careers. Our employees proudly work and serve our communities from our headquarters in Shelton, CT, across the United States and around the globe.

**Hubbell Utility Solutions**

Hubbell Utility Solutions (HUS) enable the grid to conduct, communicate and control energy across utility applications. HUS provides the critical components that allow the grid to reliably transmit and distribute energy, as well as the communications and controls technologies to make the grid smarter and more flexible.

Hubbell Incorporated, its subsidiaries and affiliates, is an EO Employer AA: M/F/Veteran/Disability. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or any other protected class.

The above summary of position responsibilities and requirements is not intended, and should not be construed, to be an exhaustive list of duties, skills, efforts, physical requirements, or working conditions associated with the position. It is intended to be an accurate reflection of those principal position elements essential for making decisions related to position performance, employee development, and compensation.

new_roles.title: Senior Manager, Warehouse Operations
new_roles.description:
**Who We Are**

Stored Energy Systems (SENS) is an award-winning manufacturer of premium quality power conversion products located in Longmont, CO. In business for over 50 years, SENS is the market leader with a proven track record of providing highly reliable battery chargers, DC power systems, and related products to industrial markets. For more information on our company please see our web site at www.sens-usa.com.

**View the SENS Product Catalog**

**Summary**

The Senior Manager, Warehouse Operations leads the people, processes, and systems that maintain accurate inventory and reliable material flow across Stored Energy Systems (SENS) manufacturing operations. Based at Disc Drive headquarters, this role leads teams and team members across all SENS locations on first shift (days) and second shift (evenings). The role oversees receiving, warehousing, inventory control, material handling, production replenishment, kitting, inter-factory transportation, shipping, and freight coordination, while developing teams and operating capacity to support production continuity, customer deliveries, and growth.

**Responsibilities**

Leadership and Operating Performance

* Establish consistent material handling and inventory management standards, performance expectations, and accountability across all locations.
* Develop supervisors and team leaders through coaching, training, performance management, and succession planning.
* Own Warehouse Operations staffing plans and coordinate coverage, priorities, and escalation processes across all locations and both shifts to support production needs.
* Promote safe material handling and consistent workplace practices in partnership with the Environmental Health and Safety team.

Inventory Accuracy and Control

* Own inventory accuracy and control standards across SENS inventory locations, including inventory held at partner locations.
* Establish consistent receiving, put-away, picking, transfer, issue, return, and reconciliation processes in Infor SyteLine. Oversee receipt processing for non-inventory purchases.
* Lead cycle counting, inventory discrepancy investigations, root-cause analysis, and corrective actions.
* Maintain material identification, traceability, first-in, first-out practices, and segregation of restricted or nonconforming inventory.
* Partner with Procurement and Finance on inventory reconciliation and actions to improve inventory health, supporting Procurement’s ownership of inventory turns, safety stock levels, and excess and obsolete inventory.
* Lead preparation and execution of annual physical inventories at all SENS locations.

Production Material Flow

* Lead production material delivery, including stock picking, replenishment of point-of-use inventory areas, scheduled material delivery routes, and kanban replenishment parameters. Align execution with sales, inventory, and operations planning (SIOP) and production schedules.
* Develop and implement scalable assembly-phase kitting processes for configure-to-order and engineer-to-order products. Ensure kit accuracy, completeness, alignment with current revisions, staging, and return of unused materials.
* Coordinate material priorities, shortage escalations, and decisions about incomplete kits with Planning, Production, and Procurement.
* Establish visual management and kanban replenishment processes from kitting through delivery to production lines.

Transportation, Shipping, and Freight

* Own inter-factory transportation and inventory transfers, movement of finished products to shipping, and return flows for empty bins, carts, and protective packing materials.
* Lead local shipping operations and centralized inbound and outbound freight execution, coordinating with Planning & Fulfillment and Order Management to support on-time, complete customer shipments.
* Manage freight and premium freight costs against budget and maintain transportation contingency plans to support production continuity and customer deliveries.

Capacity and Continuous Improvement

* Translate production forecasts into logistics capacity plans. Lead warehouse and material-flow readiness for factory expansions and production ramps, including space, staffing, and training.
* Improve productivity through standard work, waste reduction, daily performance management, process automation, and enterprise resource planning (ERP) system improvements, in partnership with IT, Manufacturing Engineering, and Continuous Improvement.

**Required Qualifications**

* 8+ years of experience in manufacturing inventory, warehousing, and logistics, including 5+ years leading supervisors and teams across multiple sites and shifts.
* Demonstrated success scaling warehouse operations in a high-growth manufacturing environment.
* Strong knowledge of inventory controls, ERP transactions, cycle counting, kanban, supermarkets, production replenishment, and order kitting.
* Experience managing shipping operations, transportation providers, and freight costs.
* Experience supporting repetitive manufacturing production.
* Demonstrated ability to improve inventory accuracy, establish consistent operating practices, and develop effective supervisors and team leaders.
* Ability to analyze operational and financial data, resolve problems, and communicate priorities and issues across functions.
* Experience implementing Lean or continuous improvement initiatives.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in supply chain, logistics, operations, engineering, or a related field
* Relevant supply chain, logistics, or Lean certification.
* Experience with Infor SyteLine, barcode scanning, and warehouse management systems.
* Experience in electrical equipment, industrial products, or similarly complex manufacturing environments.
* Experience supporting configure-to-order or engineer-to-order production.

**Location:** Longmont, CO

**Base Compensation:** $135,000 - $165,000 is the projected range of annual base salary for this role depending on the candidate’s overall qualifications and experience.

**Bonus:** This position is eligible for an annual bonus based on individual and company performance.

**Closing Date:** December 1st. While we expect to keep the position open through this date, the posting may be extended or closed early based on applicant volume and hiring needs.

**Onsite Perks**

* Free gym with 24/7 access
* Free Electric Vehicle charging
* Breakfast and Lunch Café
* After hours Grab & Go snacks
* Basketball court
* Walking paths

**Benefits**

* Paid Time Off
* Paid holidays
* Medical insurance
* Dental insurance
* Vision insurance
* Short-term and long-term disability
* Life insurance
* 401(k) plan with immediate vesting
* Employee referral program
* Tuition reimbursement
* Professional development

At SENS, our culture is rooted in a set of core values that reflect who we are and how we work. In a recent 2025 poll, our employees identified the values that best define us: *“Innovative”, “Respectful”, “Inviting”, “Flexible”, “Collaborative”, and “Growth Driven”.* Our team describes us as a dynamic, forward-thinking company where everyone has the opportunity to thrive.

We pride ourselves on being an equal opportunity employer, fully dedicated to fostering inclusion and diversity. We welcome all applicants, regardless of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, genetic information, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other legally protected characteristic.

We hope you're interested in making a difference with us. Even if you don't feel that you meet every qualification listed in this job description, we still encourage you to apply.

new_roles.title: SR. Manager Human Resources, Manufacturing (People & Culture)
new_roles.description:
**Job Description Summary:**

At The Coca-Cola Company, our people and culture are essential to how we create value, grow our business, and make a difference every day. We are looking for a **Senior Manager, Human Resources-People & Culture (Manufacturing)** who will bring strong business partnership, sound judgment, and hands-on People & Culture leadership to two manufacturing locations supporting both union and non-union associates.

 

This role is the Primary **People & Culture Leader and** visible face of **Human Resources at the plant** , serving as a trusted partner to plant leadership and an accessible resource for associates. The Senior Manager will report directly to the Plant Manager, with a dotted-line relationship to the Director, People & Culture, helping ensure strong alignment between plant priorities and broader People & Culture strategies, standards, and practices.

 

Success requires someone who can move comfortably between the plant floor and leadership discussions. You will listen to associates, coach leaders, navigate complex employee and labor relations matters, use workforce insights to inform decisions, develop talent, and translate business priorities into practical people solutions. The ideal candidate brings manufacturing Human Resources experience, labor relations capability, strong business acumen, a commitment to inclusion, and the ability to build credibility and trusted relationships at every level of the organization.

 

**Key Responsibilities and Position-Related Functions**
-------------------------------------------------------

* Serve as the senior on-site People & Culture partner for two manufacturing locations, providing hands-on leadership and support across union and non-union associate populations.
* Partner directly with the Plant Manager and plant leadership teams to translate operational and business priorities into actionable workforce, talent, culture, and organizational initiatives.
* Serve as the primary, visible People & Culture resource for associates, creating an approachable and trusted presence across shifts and levels of the organization.
* Coach and advise plant leaders on organizational effectiveness, leadership capability, performance management, accountability, employee development, workforce decisions, and people-related business challenges.
* Lead and support employee relations matters with objectivity, consistency, confidentiality, sound judgment, and appropriate partnership with the Director, People & Culture and other subject-matter experts.
* Support labor relations within the unionized location, including interpretation and consistent application of the collective bargaining agreement, issue resolution, grievance processes, and development of productive labor-management relationships.
* Partner with leaders to promote a positive, inclusive, safe, and respectful workplace where associates can contribute, grow, and thrive.
* Lead workforce planning discussions, using workforce data and operational insights to identify talent needs, retention risks, organizational opportunities, and appropriate actions.
* Strengthen leader capability in performance management, associate engagement, development conversations, conflict resolution, and consistent application of People & Culture practices.
* Partner with leaders on talent reviews, succession planning, career development, critical-role planning, and development opportunities that build plant capability.
* Support recruiting and selection activities in partnership with Talent Acquisition and plant leaders, including workforce requirements, candidate assessment, pre-employment activities, and an effective transition from candidate to associate.
* Lead and continuously improve new-hire onboarding and integration, helping new associates understand performance expectations, workplace culture, policies, resources, and ways of working.
* Provide guidance to associates and leaders on pay, benefits, leave, workplace policies, Human Resources programs, systems, and processes, engaging appropriate partners when specialized expertise is required.
* Analyze turnover, attendance, staffing, engagement, workforce demographics, and other people data to identify trends and translate insights into practical recommendations for plant leadership.
* Apply digital tools, automation, and artificial intelligence responsibly to improve People & Culture insights, efficiency, associate experience, and decision-making while maintaining appropriate confidentiality and data stewardship.
* Ensure People & Culture practices and documentation are consistent with company policies, applicable collective bargaining agreements, and employment and labor requirements.
* Maintain accurate and appropriate associate records, documentation, systems, and reporting, with a strong focus on data integrity and confidentiality.
* Partner closely with the Director, People & Culture, keeping them informed of material plant activities, emerging workforce risks, labor and employee relations matters, and issues requiring escalation or broader functional support.
* Lead or support People & Culture programs, change initiatives, communications, events, and projects that strengthen organizational effectiveness and the associate experience across both locations.
Build effective partnerships across the broader People & Culture network and plant functions to solve problems, implement change, and deliver sustainable business and people outcomes. 

 

**Education and Qualifications**
--------------------------------

* Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Industrial or Labor Relations, Organizational Development, or a related field.
* 7+ years of progressive Human Resources experience, with meaningful experience supporting manufacturing, supply chain, distribution, or another complex operational environment.
* Demonstrated experience supporting both **union and non-union employee populations** , including practical knowledge of labor relations, collective bargaining agreements, grievance management, and consistent contract administration.
* Experience serving as a trusted Human Resources partner to senior operational leaders and translating business priorities into effective people solutions.
* Strong employee relations capability, including experience evaluating complex workplace situations, conducting or supporting investigations, resolving conflict, managing risk, and determining when escalation or specialist partnership is appropriate.
* Strong working knowledge of employment practices, labor relations principles, performance management, leave practices, and Human Resources policy interpretation.
* Experience supporting hourly and salaried populations and building credibility with associates and leaders across multiple organizational levels and work schedules.
* Demonstrated capability in workforce planning, talent management, succession planning, associate engagement, organizational effectiveness, and leader development.
* Strong data literacy with the ability to interpret workforce metrics, identify meaningful trends, develop insights, and use evidence to influence business decisions.
* Digital fluency across Human Resources information systems and productivity platforms; experience with UKG/Kronos or comparable workforce management technology is preferred.
* Practical understanding of responsible artificial intelligence use and an ability to identify opportunities to apply digital and AI-enabled solutions to People & Culture work while protecting confidential associate information.
* Strong communication, coaching, influencing, facilitation, conflict-resolution, and relationship-building skills.
* Demonstrated ability to manage competing priorities, exercise sound judgment, maintain confidentiality, and make timely decisions in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
* Ability to lead through change, navigate ambiguity, and build alignment among stakeholders with different perspectives and priorities.
* Demonstrated commitment to fostering an inclusive workplace in which associates are treated with dignity and respect and have opportunities to contribute and develop.
* Ability to build productive partnerships across two locations while maintaining a strong, visible presence with plant leadership and associates.
Human Resources professional certification, such as SHRM-CP, SHRM-SCP, PHR, or SPHR, is valued but not required. 

The Coca-Cola Company will not offer sponsorship for employment status (including, but not limited to, H1-B visa status and other employment-based nonimmigrant visas) for this position. Accordingly, all applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis and must not require The Coca-Cola Company's sponsorship to continue to work legally in the United States.

**Skills:**

Analytics Insights, Human Resources Policies, Human Resources Training, Leadership, Strategic Human Resources Leadership, Waterfall Model

**Pay Range:**

United States: 130,000 - 147,000 USD


*Base pay offered may vary depending on geography, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. A full range of medical, financial, and/or other benefits, dependent on the position, is offered.*

**Location(s):**

United States of America

**City/Cities:**

Ontario

**Travel Required:**

00% - 25%

**Relocation Provided:**

No

**Job Posting End Date:**

November 27, 2026

**Our Purpose and Growth Culture:**

We are taking deliberate action to nurture an inclusive culture that is grounded in our company purpose, to refresh the world and make a difference. We act with a growth mindset, take an expansive approach to what’s possible and believe in continuous learning to improve our business and ourselves. We focus on four key behaviors – curious, empowered, inclusive and agile – and value how we work as much as what we achieve. We believe that our culture is one of the reasons our company continues to thrive after 130+ years. Visit Our Purpose and Vision to learn more about these behaviors and how you can bring them to life in your next role at Coca-Cola.

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and do not discriminate against any employee or applicant for employment because of race, color, sex, age, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity and/or expression, status as a veteran, and basis of disability or any other federal, state or local protected class. When we collect your personal information as part of a job application or offer of employment, we do so in accordance with industry standards and best practices and in compliance with applicable privacy laws.

new_roles.title: Senior Manager Production
new_roles.description:
**Career Area:**

Manufacturing

**Job Description:**

**Your Work Shapes the World at Caterpillar Inc.**

When you join Caterpillar, you're joining a global team who cares not just about the work we do – but also about each other. We are the makers, problem solvers, and future world builders who are creating stronger, more sustainable communities. We don't just talk about progress and innovation here – we make it happen, with our customers, where we work and live. Together, we are building a better world, so we can all enjoy living in it.

Caterpillar is seeking a **Senior Manager Production** to provide senior leadership for production operations at our Griffin Engine Packaging Plant. This role serves as a key production leader responsible for overseeing genset and power module manufacturing operations in a fast-paced, high-velocity production environment.

As the leader of a team consisting of seven direct-report supervisors and multiple indirect reports, you will drive operational performance across safety, quality, productivity, and cost objectives while creating an environment focused on employee development and operational excellence.

This position offers the opportunity to lead large-scale power systems production operations, overseeing products ranging from approximately 400 kVA to 4 MW. The successful candidate will champion a safety-first culture, support lean manufacturing initiatives, and provide leadership for day-to-day operational execution and continuous improvement efforts.

### **How You Will Make an Impact**

* **Safety-Driven Culture** - Lead with a safety-first mindset and drive a culture where safety is the top operational priority.
* **Operational Excellence** - Deliver strong manufacturing performance through effective management of safety, quality, productivity, and cost objectives.
* **People Leadership and Development** - Develop, coach, and support leaders while building organizational capability across the production team.
* **Lean Manufacturing Leadership** - Champion lean manufacturing principles and continuous improvement initiatives that enhance operational performance.
* **Large-Scale Power Systems Production** - Provide leadership for genset and power module production operations supporting a complex manufacturing environment.

Responsibilities include:

* Leading production operations within a high-velocity manufacturing environment.
* Driving safety performance and fostering a safety-first culture throughout the organization.
* Managing competing priorities related to safety, quality, productivity, and cost.
* Leading employee development activities and performance management processes.
* Resolving day-to-day operational escalations and manufacturing challenges.
* Supporting lean manufacturing and continuous improvement initiatives.
* Overseeing genset and power module production operations.; emphasis on NPI operational support (i.e headcount, capacity planning, etc...)

### **Degree Requirement**

Bachelor's Degree or equivalent experience.

### **What Skills You Will Have**

**Production Training:** Extensive knowledge of approaches, tools and techniques for delivering formal and informal training on the safe and efficient operation of production machinery; ability to conduct effective formal and situation-specific training.

**Problem Solving:** Extensive knowledge of approaches, tools, techniques for recognizing, anticipating, and resolving organizational, operational or process problems; ability to apply knowledge of problem solving appropriately to diverse situations

**Influencing:** Extensive knowledge of effective influencing tactics and strategies; ability to impact decisions within and outside own organization.

**Flexibility and Adaptability:** Extensive knowledge of successful approaches and techniques for dealing with change; ability to adapt to a changing environment and be comfortable with change.

**Performance Management:** Extensive knowledge of successful performance management techniques; ability to apply organization's performance management system, practices, and tools to developing and improving individual, team, and organizational performance.

**Analytical Thinking:** Extensive knowledge of techniques and tools that promote effective analysis; ability to determine the root cause of organizational problems and create alternative solutions that resolve these problems.

**Planning and Organizing:** Extensive knowledge of the process of planning and arranging tasks and resources; ability to plan and organize both time and resources to get things completed while structuring and maintaining work in a systematic and highly methodical way.

**Effective Communications:** Extensive understanding of effective communication concepts, tools and techniques; ability to effectively transmit, receive, and accurately interpret ideas, information, and needs through the application of appropriate communication behaviors.

**Leadership & People Management:** Extensive understanding of the techniques and skills needed to lead in the production environment; with the demonstrated ability to develop talent using performance management techniques

### **Top Candidates Will Also Have**

* Experiences as a leader of leaders; specifically in cross-functional teams with support staff
* Manufacturing experience in the product producing environment; preference for heavy equipment, automotive, aerospace, rail, or other closely related industries.
* Examples of contributing to or leading manufacturing process transformation
* LEAN/Six Sigma Certification.

### **Additional Information**

* **Location:** Griffin, Georgia
* **Work Arrangement:** Onsite
* **Relocation:** Available
* **Travel:** Less than 10%
* **Sponsorship:** Not available

#LI

**Summary Pay Range:**

$147,760.00 - $221,640.00

Compensation and benefits offered may vary depending on multiple individualized factors, job level, market location, job-related knowledge, skills, individual performance and experience. Please note that salary is only one component of total compensation at Caterpillar.

**Benefits:**

Subject to plan eligibility, terms, and guidelines. This is a summary list of benefits.

* Medical, dental, and vision benefits\*
* Paid time off plan (Vacation, Holidays, Volunteer, etc.)\*
* 401(k) savings plans\*
* Health Savings Account (HSA)\*
* Flexible Spending Accounts (FSAs)\*
* Health Lifestyle Programs\*
* Employee Assistance Program\*
* Voluntary Benefits and Employee Discounts\*
* Career Development\*
* Incentive bonus\*
* Disability benefits
* Life Insurance
* Parental leave
* Adoption benefits
* Tuition Reimbursement

* These benefits also apply to part-time employees

This position requires working onsite five days a week.Relocation is available for this position.Visa Sponsorship is not available for this position.

**Posting Dates:**

November 11, 2026 - November 18, 2026

Any offer of employment is conditioned upon the successful completion of a drug screen.

Caterpillar is an Equal Opportunity Employer, Including Veterans and Individuals with Disabilities. Qualified applicants of any age are encouraged to apply.

At RTX, the world's largest aerospace and defense company, 185,000 great minds are united by purpose and inspired to make a difference solving the world’s most complex problems. With our three market leading businesses, world-class operations and investments in research and development, we offer capabilities and opportunity no one else can. Together, we push the boundaries of known science and find new ways to connect and protect our world.

Raytheon brings the strength of more than 100 years of experience and renowned engineering expertise to meet the needs of today’s mission and stay ahead of tomorrow’s threat. We deliver solutions that help our nation and allies defend freedoms and deter aggression, creating a safer, more secure world. Join us and help shape the future of aerospace and defense.

Raytheon has an opening for a Sr. Production Control Lead supporting our Undersea Factory in our Portsmouth, RI facility. The successful candidate has experience with Material Requirements Planning (MRP) systems in a manufacturing environment and utilizes data-driven decision making to enable effective material and workforce forecasting. This role requires daily interaction with cross functional teams, programs, and business units to maintain and meet organizational goals and objectives. These groups include planning, production control, operations, quality, and manufacturing/test/design engineering.

**What You Will Do**

* Managing a highly visible area with 6 production control professionals reporting into this position.
* Set strategic vision, direction and plan to execute on short to medium term program and functional strategies and initiatives.
* Material Availability Analysis, Tracking, and Reporting.
* Manage Kit Readiness including working with cross-functional team in BOM, Material Master, Process Engineering, Operations, and Document Control.
* Releasing production schedules in multiple tools through the MRP system and confirming in shop floor system.
* Coordinates kitting process with multiple stores and consolidation areas.
* Provide production floor support including replacement part management, shop floor material staging, Work in Progress (WIP) movement through shared resource areas, completion of units in shop floor and MRP system, delivery to next step (inventory or shipment), and meeting MRP schedule.
* Control the physical disposition of nonconforming or specially handled material including Return to Vendor, purged material, WIP STOP per contractual restrictions, and configuration of components/sub-assemblies as required.
* Maintain integrity of the shop floor, MRP, and inventory systems through key performance metrics.
* Process piece part movement to support internal build requirements through subcontractors, internal shared resources, and other Raytheon Technologies facilities.
* This position is an onsite role in our Portsmouth, RI facility.

**Qualifications You Must Have**

* Typically requires A University Degree or equivalent experience and minimum 10 years prior relevant experience, or An Advanced Degree in a related field and minimum 7 years experience.
* Experience in Production Control, Supply Chain, Planning, Logistics, Scheduling, Operations, Manufacturing, or other production driven environments within manufacturing.
* Experience with MRP/ERP systems.
* Experience leading daily team operations and/or comparable leadership experience.

**Qualifications We Prefer**

* Experience leading in a Department of Defense (DoD) environment.
* Experience in Special Program Access and other business systems, including shop floor data systems.
* Experience in Six Sigma, CORE, Lean Manufacturing processes, diagnostics, and continuous improvement.
* Experience driving financial performance, cost reduction, staffing, and budgeting.

**What We Offer**

* Our values drive our actions, behaviors, and performance with a vision for a safer, more connected world. At RTX we value: Safety, Trust, Respect, Accountability, Collaboration, and Innovation.

**Learn More & Apply Now!**

* **Please consider the following role type definition as you apply for this role.**
 + **Onsite:** Employees who are working in Onsite roles will work primarily onsite. This includes all production and maintenance employees, as they are essential to the development of our products.
* **Clearance Information:** This position requires a security clearance. **DCSA Consolidated Adjudication Services (DCSA CAS)**, an agency of the Department of Defense, handles and adjudicates the security clearance process. More information about Security Clearances can be found on the US Department of State government website here: https://www.state.gov/m/ds/clearances/c10978.htm

***As part of our commitment to maintaining a secure hiring process, candidates may be asked to attend select steps of the interview process in-person at one of our office locations, regardless of whether the role is designated as on-site, hybrid or remote.***

The salary range for this role is 132,400 USD - 251,600 USD. The salary range provided is a good faith estimate representative of all experience levels. RTX considers several factors when extending an offer, including but not limited to, the role, function and associated responsibilities, a candidate’s work experience, location, education/training, and key skills.Hired applicants may be eligible for benefits, including but not limited to, medical, dental, vision, life insurance, short-term disability, long-term disability, 401(k) match, flexible spending accounts, flexible work schedules, employee assistance program, Employee Scholar Program, parental leave, paid time off, and holidays. Specific benefits are dependent upon the specific business unit as well as whether or not the position is covered by a collective-bargaining agreement.Hired applicants may be eligible for annual short-term and/or long-term incentive compensation programs depending on the level of the position and whether or not it is covered by a collective-bargaining agreement. Payments under these annual programs are not guaranteed and are dependent upon a variety of factors including, but not limited to, individual performance, business unit performance, and/or the company’s performance.This role is a U.S.-based role. If the successful candidate resides in a U.S. territory, the appropriate pay structure and benefits will apply.RTX anticipates the application window closing approximately 40 days from the date the notice was posted. However, factors such as candidate flow and business necessity may require RTX to shorten or extend the application window.

*RTX is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability or veteran status, or any other applicable state or federal protected class. RTX provides affirmative action in employment for qualified Individuals with a Disability and Protected Veterans in compliance with Section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act and the Vietnam Era Veterans’ Readjustment Assistance Act.*

new_roles.title: Plant Manager
new_roles.description:
**Company Description**

Sirtex Medical is a global leader in healthcare, with offices in the U.S., Australia, Germany, and Singapore, dedicated to improving patient outcomes.

Our mission is to be at the forefront of minimally invasive cancer and embolization therapies. By partnering with physicians, we aim to provide innovative products that enhance patient outcomes and simplify treatments. Achieving this ambitious goal requires passionate and talented individuals who are committed to making a difference. Our flagship product, SIR-Spheres® Y-90 resin microspheres, is a targeted radiation therapy for liver cancer. To date, we have delivered over >150K doses across 50+ countries, significantly impacting patients' lives worldwide. Our success is fueled by our dedication to serving the medical community, maintaining professionalism, fostering a collaborative work culture, nurturing an entrepreneurial spirit, and continuously pursuing innovation and improvement.

At Sirtex, we are committed to creating a great workplace. We offer a range of benefits, programs, and services to support our employees, ensuring they have opportunities to contribute to our success and advance their careers. Join our inclusive community, where you can collaborate with talented colleagues, bring your ideas to life, and advance your career, all while delivering innovative healthcare solutions to patients.

 **Job Description**

**SCOPE:**

The Wilmington plant is the largest of 3 global Sirtex manufacturing site and serves as the principal production site of both SIR-Spheres microspheres and Lava product lines. The Plant Manager is responsible for leading the sites manufacturing operations, engineering, warehouse and product distribution.

**PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES:**

 

* Develop and lead execution of the site manufacturing strategy for both the SIR-Spheres and Lava value streams. Align site goals with Senior Leadership and Corporate objectives.
* Team Performance Management: lead, develop and mentor manufacturing team members.
* Manage production schedules, ensuring resource availability and capacity to meet demand, working closely with the Supply Chain team, using optimal schedules to minimize overall costs.
* Lead Continuous Improvement efforts, identifying process, equipment, product, and other opportunities, that reduce cost, improve quality and safety at the site.
* Full responsibility for developing and managing to site budget.
* Ensure resource and equipment capacity to ensure efficient and reliable manufacturing.
* Set site target KPI’s managing OEE, Labor Efficiency, Scrap, Equipment Utilization, etc.
* Ensure product is built to specification and in compliance with all Quality System requirements.
* Manage the site engineering team to ensure equipment and processes are robust and meet all manufacturing requirements. Manage PM strategy and ensure that execution is completed on time.
* Support the Quality Department, working with on site Quality team members to ensure that compliance with all areas of the Sirtex QMS are being followed. Identify opportunities for improvement and work to implement them directly in the QMS.
* Work in conjunction with HSE/Facilities Department to ensure a safe working environment for all employees and that the facilities is maintained, and compliant with regulatory requirements for both the handling of radioactive materials and medical device manufacturing.
* Manage all shipping, receiving and warehousing activities. Ensure timely material receipt, inventory accuracy is maintained, and products are shipped on time.

 
**Qualifications**

**EDUCATIONAL PREREQUISITES AND SKILL REQUIREMENTS:**

* Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering or related discipline such as Chemistry or Biomedical field
* 5+ Years experience working in medical device or pharmaceutical industry preferred.
* Prior experience working with radioisotopes preferred.
* 3+ years of site management experience, with 10+ years of leadership experience.
* 6 Sigma Green belt preferred. Experience using 5S and Lean principles is preferred.

The anticipated annual base salary range and target bonus opportunity is $136,000 to $171,000 annually, plus a 15% target annual bonus.

The final position level and compensation will be determined based on non-discriminatory, job-related factors, including geographic location, skills, experience, education, and alignment with the position requirements. In addition to base salary and bonus eligibility, Sirtex offers a comprehensive benefits package, including paid sick and vacation time, medical, dental, vision and life insurance, and a generous 401(k) matching program and other benefits, subject to applicable plan terms and eligibility requirements.

 **Additional Information**

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines

Do you want to be part of something bigger? A team whose impact stretches across the globe making a real difference to the quality of people’s lives. Sirtex recognizes that well-being, financial health, and work-life balance are crucial for our employees to achieve personal success.

Sirtex offers qualified candidates:

* Diverse and flexible work arrangements to achieve the optimum balance between work and personal responsibilities.
* A culture of respect, diversity, collaboration, and innovation fostering inclusiveness and superior performance.
* Attractive compensation and benefit packages which are practical, robust and equitable.
* A commitment to support ongoing professional growth through career development, on the job experiences and training opportunities.
* Challenging work which supports the development of new and better ways to improve clinical outcomes for oncology treatment around the world.
* An unwavering commitment to company values, employee safety and excellence in everything we do.

Diversity drives innovation; inclusion fosters belonging, growth and success. Sirtex believes that it takes multiple perspectives and voices to create a culture and workplace which fosters engagement, teamwork, and employee satisfaction to perform our best and deliver on commitments. We are dedicated to fostering an environment where all employees feel valued, included, and can share their ideas so that we can exceed even our own expectations.

Sirtex is An Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or veteran status, age or any other characteristic protected under applicable law. Sirtex will make reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with known disabilities, in accordance with applicable law.

new_roles.title: Senior Manager of Production
new_roles.description:
Gwynedd Manufacturing is seeking a hands-on Senior Manager of Production with a strong CNC machining background to lead day-to-day operations in a high-precision environment. This role is ideal for someone who has progressed through the ranks—from the shop floor into leadership—and is ready to step into a broader operational role.

The ideal candidate brings deep, practical knowledge of CNC machining (mills, lathes, EDM) and thrives in a fast-paced, high-tolerance manufacturing setting. This is not a purely strategic role—this leader will be actively engaged on the floor, driving performance, mentoring teams, and continuously improving processes.

Key Responsibilities:

* Lead daily plant operations with a strong presence on the manufacturing floor, ensuring output, quality, and efficiency targets are met
* Direct oversight of machining operations including CNC mills, lathes, and EDM, ensuring optimal machine utilization and performance
* Manage and develop a team of supervisors, leads, and machinists (50–100+ employees)
* Serve as a technical resource and mentor, supporting setup, programming, and troubleshooting when needed
* Drive continuous improvement initiatives focused on cycle time reduction, scrap reduction, and process standardization
* Partner closely with Engineering and Quality to ensure tight tolerance requirements and manufacturability of parts
* Own production scheduling, workflow optimization, and labor planning to meet customer demand
* Establish and reinforce shop floor accountability, KPIs, and standard work practices
* Maintain a safe, compliant, and disciplined manufacturing environment
* Support new product introductions and prototype builds with a strong understanding of machining constraints
* Overseeing multiple departments withing the manufacturing space.

Qualifications:

* 5+ years of progressive manufacturing experience, with clear growth from hands-on machining into leadership
* Strong CNC background required (setup, programming, and/or machining experience with mills, lathes, EDM)
* Prior experience in roles such as Machine Shop Manager, Manufacturing Manager, or Plant Manager
* Proven ability to lead teams in a high-precision, tight-tolerance environment
* Deep understanding of machining processes, tooling, fixturing, and production workflows
* Experience driving continuous improvement on the shop floor (Lean, process optimization, etc.)
* Comfortable being hands-on and highly visible in daily operations, not just managing from an office
* Strong leadership and communication skills with the ability to develop talent from within
* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or related field preferred, but equivalent hands-on experience strongly valued

Physical and Work Environment Requirements: 
This position is based in a manufacturing environment and may require the following over extended periods of time up to a full 8-hour work shift (excluding lunch and breaks): stand, walk, sit, squat or bend, kneel and rise, lift, carry, push, or pull materials and equipment weighing up to — and occasionally exceeding — 50 pounds, view a computer or other digital screen, work on a computer, workstation or comparable system, and make accurate entries in such systems. Manual dexterity and fine motor skills are required for detailed assembly and precision work. Work may take place in areas with varying temperatures or no climate control, varying noise levels, and production equipment in motion. Proper personal protective equipment (PPE) must be worn in designated areas at all times as required by company policy. Reasonable accommodations may be available to enable individuals with disabilities but are always subject to safety concerns for the employee and all team members. Employer may require a physical assessment of the candidate’s ability to perform these tasks as a condition of an offer letter. Any assessment will be performed by a third party vendor and will be reported on a pass/fail basis with no other medical information conveyed to employer.

*Equal Opportunity Employer:* 
*Gwynedd Manufacturing is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws.*

*Note: This job description reflects general duties and responsibilities and is not intended to be an exhaustive list. Management may modify or assign other responsibilities as needed.*

new_roles.title: Director of Insurance Operations
new_roles.description:
**Foundation Risk Partners****, one of the fastest growing insurance brokerage and consulting firms in the US, is adding a** ***Director of Operations-Insurance*** **to their team in** ***Lakeland, FL.***

**Job Summary:**

The Commercial Lines Operations Leader is responsible for overseeing the operational effectiveness, service delivery, and strategic execution of commercial lines insurance processes. This role ensures alignment with business goals, regulatory compliance, and a high standard of customer and broker satisfaction. The leader will drive continuous improvement, operational efficiency, and team performance across underwriting support, policy servicing, and client onboarding.

**Essential Functions:**

* **Operational Leadership:** 
 Lead day-to-day operations for commercial lines, ensuring timely and accurate processing of policies, endorsements, renewals, and cancellations.
* **Process Optimization:** 
 Identify and implement process improvements to enhance efficiency, accuracy, and scalability of operations.
* **Team Management:** 
 Manage and develop a high-performing team, including training, performance management, and career development.
* **Cross-Functional Collaboration:** 
 Partner with underwriting, claims, IT, compliance, and sales teams to ensure seamless service delivery and operational alignment.
* **Technology & Automation:** 
 Leverage technology and automation tools to streamline workflows and reduce manual tasks.
* **Compliance & Risk Management:** 
 Ensure adherence to regulatory requirements, internal controls, and company policies.
* **Reporting & Analytics:** 
 Monitor KPIs, service levels, and operational metrics to drive data-informed decisions and continuous improvement.
* **Customer Experience:** 
 Champion a customer-first mindset, ensuring high service standards for brokers, agents, and policyholders.

**Competencies & Qualifications:**

* 7+ years of experience in insurance operations
* Proven leadership experience managing teams and driving operational excellence
* Strong knowledge of insurance products, systems, and regulatory environment
* Excellent communication, analytical, and problem-solving skills
* Change management and process improvement expertise

**Education & Experience:**

* Bachelor's degree in Business, Insurance, or related field preferred
* Experience with insurance platforms (e.g. Applied Epic)
 

**Disclaimer:**

While this job description is intended to be an accurate reflection of the job requirements, management reserves the right to modify, add, or remove duties from particular jobs and to assign other duties as necessary.

**Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO):**

FRP provides equal employment opportunity to qualified persons regardless of race, color, sex, religion, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, veteran status, or any other classifications protected by law.

**Benefits:**

FRP offers a comprehensive range of health-related benefit options including medical, vision, and dental. We offer a 401(k) with company match, company paid life insurance, STD, LTD and a generous PTO policy starting at 18 days per year plus 10 paid holidays & 2 floating holidays!

new_roles.title: Director - Service Operations
new_roles.description:
As the **Director of Service Operations** at Lumos, you'll play a critical leadership role in delivering reliable fiber connectivity and an exceptional customer experience across our growing markets. You'll lead and develop regional operations teams, oversee service installations and maintenance, and drive the performance, safety, and efficiency of our field operations.

This is an opportunity to make a meaningful impact as Lumos continues to expand, combining strategic leadership with hands-on operational expertise to strengthen service delivery, improve processes, and build high-performing teams that support our customers and continued growth.

This is a remote position supporting Service Operations across the Midwest region, with a preference for candidates located within a Lumos market in **Ohio, Indiana, or Kentucky**. Regional travel is required.

**Why Lumos:**

Lumos is transforming the future of connectivity by building one of the nation's fastest-growing 100% Fiber Optic networks. Through T-Fiber, our joint venture with T-Mobile, we're working toward a shared goal of connecting 12 to 15 million homes by 2030 while expanding access to reliable, high-speed internet in the communities we serve.

Here, you'll find more than a job, you'll have the opportunity to make an impact, take ownership of your work, and help shape how we grow. We move quickly, collaborate across teams, and believe the best ideas come from people who are curious, solutions-oriented, and ready to build what's next.

**What You'll Do:**

* Lead, coach, and develop regional Service Operations managers and teams, fostering accountability, collaboration, and a strong customer-first culture.
* Oversee service installations, maintenance, and field operations across assigned markets, ensuring consistent quality, safety, and operational performance.
* Establish and monitor KPIs, SLAs, and customer experience metrics to drive efficiency, service reliability, and continuous improvement.
* Develop and execute operational strategies that support market expansion, service delivery objectives, and long-term business growth.
* Manage department budgets, resources, and operational projects to ensure effective planning, execution, and cost management.
* Oversee vendor and contractor performance, including negotiations, service expectations, and accountability for operational results.
* Serve as a key escalation point for complex customer and operational challenges, driving timely resolution and improvements to the customer experience.
* Partner across Network Operations, Engineering, Construction, Customer Care, and other teams to improve workflows, strengthen service delivery, and support business objectives.
* Establish and maintain operational policies, procedures, and safety standards while identifying opportunities to improve processes and scale operations.

**What You'll Bring:**

* 7+ years of experience in telecommunications service operations, field operations, or a related area.
* Proven experience leading geographically dispersed teams, developing managers, and driving operational performance across multiple markets.
* Strong understanding of telecommunications service installation, maintenance, network operations, and customer service delivery.
* Experience managing operational budgets, vendor relationships, contractor performance, and service-level agreements.
* Ability to analyze KPIs, operational performance, and customer satisfaction metrics to identify trends and drive improvements.
* Strong leadership, communication, problem-solving, and decision-making skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office and operational software platforms, with the ability to adapt to new systems and technologies.
* A proactive, solutions-oriented approach with the ability to work independently and lead effectively in a fast-paced environment.

**What Makes You a Great Fit:**

* High school diploma or equivalent.
* Bachelor's degree in business, telecommunications, engineering, or a related field.
* Direct experience in the fiber broadband or FTTH industry, including distributed and centralized split network architectures.
* Knowledge of central office infrastructure, network equipment, and telecommunications facilities.
* Experience improving customer satisfaction, NPS scores, and operational efficiency across multiple markets.
* A track record of developing high-performing teams, improving operational processes, and supporting growth in a scaling organization.
* A collaborative, hands-on leadership style with the ability to balance strategic priorities with day-to-day operational execution.

**Physical Requirements:**

* Frequently operates a computer, phone, and standard office tools.
* Ability to travel to properties and regional offices as needed.
* Near-constant use of sight, speech, hearing, comprehension, and reasoning.
* Must be able to sit or remain in a stationary position for extended periods.

**Benefits & Perks:**

Our commitment to communities includes recruiting and rewarding the Lumos team members who are working together to build a brighter tomorrow.

We have:

* Comprehensive health, dental, and vision coverage.
* Competitive compensation packages, including bonus options for eligible positions.
* Paid Time Off & Paid Holidays.
* Health Savings Accounts (HSAs) and Flexible Spending Accounts (FSAs).
* 100% employer-paid life and disability insurance.
* Employee Assistance Program (EAP) with access to professional support for life's challenges.
* 401K plan w/ up to 5% employer contribution and a self-directed brokerage option.
* Wellness program offering education and cash incentives for gym attendance and nutrition programs.
* Employee referral bonuses.
* Discounts on Lumos Fiber Internet for employees who live in our service areas.
* Discounts on T-Mobile wireless service and select features for lines.

**Applicant Eligibility Notice:** 
Applicants must be at least eighteen (18) years of age at the time of application.

**At Lumos we recruit, hire, employ, train, promote, and compensate individuals based on job-related qualifications and abilities. We have a longstanding policy of providing a work environment that respects the dignity and worth of each individual and is free from all forms of employment discrimination, including harassment, because of race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws. We will provide reasonable accommodation to qualified individuals** **with disabilities or based on a sincerely held religious belief, in accordance with applicable laws.**

new_roles.title: Regional Director Operations-RD
new_roles.description:
The Regional Director of Operations is responsible for providing operational leadership, client partnership support, and strategic oversight for multiple senior living dining and hospitality accounts within an assigned region. This position partners closely with community leadership teams, culinary operations, resident experience teams, and corporate leadership to ensure operational excellence, financial performance, hospitality culture, regulatory compliance, and elevated resident satisfaction across all assigned communities.

Position Type and Expected Hours of Work

This is an exempt salaried position, with expected hours to include: days, evenings, weekends, and holidays.

Essential Functions and Duties

Operational Leadership

* Provide leadership and operational oversight for multiple senior living dining and hospitality accounts
* Support and mentor Directors of Dining Services, Executive Chefs, Resident Experience leaders, and community management teams
* Ensure operational consistency, hospitality standards, and service excellence throughout all assigned communities
* Conduct regular operational visits, audits, and performance reviews

Client & Resident Relationships

* Build and maintain strong relationships with client leadership teams, residents, families, and operational partners
* Ensure resident satisfaction initiatives and hospitality-focused service culture remain a top operational priority
* Participate in client meetings, operational reviews, and strategic planning discussions
* Address operational concerns and support service recovery initiatives when needed

Financial Management

* Manage regional financial performance including:

* labor management,
* food cost controls,
* budgeting,
* forecasting,
* and overall account profitability

* Analyze financial reports and operational metrics to identify opportunities for improvement
* Support implementation of operational efficiencies and cost-control initiatives

Culinary & Hospitality Excellence

* Support culinary innovation, menu development, dining presentation, and hospitality-driven service initiatives
* Ensure dining environments reflect company hospitality standards and resident experience expectations
* Promote elevated dining experiences throughout all communities

Associate Leadership & Development

* Recruit, coach, mentor, and develop operational leadership teams
* Support associate engagement, retention, succession planning, and performance management initiatives
* Foster a positive, professional, and accountability-driven culture throughout the region
* Assist with onboarding and transition support for new business and leadership changes

Compliance & Quality Assurance

* Ensure compliance with all federal, state, local, and company regulations and standards
* Support sanitation, food safety, healthcare compliance, and regulatory audit readiness
* Conduct operational assessments and quality assurance reviews
* Ensure corrective action plans are implemented and maintained when necessary

Travel

This role will be 80-100% travel. Travel will be by car and/or plane and will include overnight travel.

General Responsibility as Required for Position

The Regional Director of Operations serves as the primary operational leader supporting community-level Directors, Executive Chefs, and management teams while helping drive consistency, service excellence, associate engagement, and overall client satisfaction throughout the region. new_roles.title: Regional Director of Operations
new_roles.description:
Circle of Life is growing, and we have an opening for a Regional Director of Operations to join our team. This position will oversee and manage our New Mexico branches; Albuquerque, Gallup, Kirtland, Shiprock, and Zuni.

**Good for employees**

Circle of Life’s focus is creating a workplace where respect, appreciation and teamwork are the shared experiences of our team. We do good for our employees by collaborating on scheduling, a focus on wellbeing, a client-first directive, respecting and valuing every team member, having fun along with top industry compensation and benefits.

**Good deeds**

We also do good in our work. Our team of office and field staff care about each other and the clients we serve. We help one another. We care and provide for a wide range of patients with a focus on serving the underserved.

**Position duties include**

* Participate in the hiring and training of managers
* Organize and oversee the work and schedules of managers
* Conduct performance evaluations
* Handle discipline of employees as needed following company policy
* Establish quantitative and qualitative metrics, guidelines, and standards by which the company's efficiency and effectiveness can be evaluated (identify opportunities for improvement)
* Implement policies and procedures that will improve day-to-day operations
* Oversee office operations, ensuring each branch is reaching goals set by departmental and company leadership
* Monitors budget and revenue in each office to achieve financial objectives
* Communicates and explains new directives, policies/procedures to manager for change and meets with staff to explain changes, answer questions, and maintain morale
* Improve customer service and satisfaction
* Market current products to potential clients, families, case workers and potential referral sources
* Leads coordination and integration of efforts among homecare teams to produce smoother workflow and more cost-effective business processes
* Traveling is required

**Qualifications**

Qualified applicants will have 3 years of management experience, excellent verbal and written communication skills and interpersonal and customer service skills. Healthcare and/or home care experience preferred. The Regional Director of Operations oversees the day-to-day activities for their assigned branches, ensuring the organization is managed and performing efficiently and effectively. While carrying out the responsibilities of the position, ensure the values of servant-leadership, empathy, altruism, and integrity are evident in all actions and encounters.

**How good?**

* Positively change the lives of individuals and families in our communities
* Serve the underserved providing access to care for those who have been traditionally overlooked by the health care system
* Support a talented team of administrative and clinical professionals and be a part of a team that supports each other

**Full Benefits include**

* Medical, Dental, 401K, Paid Holidays, Top PTO Plan, Mileage, Flexible Schedules, Vision, Year-End Bonus

new_roles.title: Director of Production
new_roles.description:
MHI Ship Repair & Services is a major marine repair and conversion contractor serving the U.S. Navy, Military Sealift Command, Maritime Administration and Commercial ship owners and operators worldwide. Our shipyard is conveniently located in the Mid-Atlantic region at the port of Hampton Roads, Norfolk Virginia.

**JOB SUMMARY:** Manages the operations of all production trades to include Facilities and Gas Free. Responsible for ensuring that all projects are manned with competent, properly trained and certified personnel, and the work efforts are coordinated and executed in a cost-effective manner, safely, and on time. Provides leadership and guidance to Shop Superintendants and oversees the maintenance and improvement of all shop equipment and development of shop procedures.

**SUPERVISES:** All Shop Superintendents

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:**

* Primary oversight of all production departments to include Facilities and Gas Free. Responsible for making strategic and tactical decisions related to certain aspects of MHI's production business to include operation non-Program work
* Responsible for ensuring that all projects are manned with competent, properly trained and certified personnel, and that work efforts are prioritized, coordinated and efforts integrated between departments and executed safely, in a cost-effective manner and on time.
* Ensures performance is within the guidelines of the contracts, delivery orders are received and that all contractual requirements are within the scope of work for the specific market and are met for U.S. Navy, Government, private shipyard, and commercial projects.
* Holds daily production meetings with all trades and Project Managers. Communicate with all department heads to ensure that any manning, scheduling, tooling, and material issues are identified and resolved.
* Attend all SRA Production Meetings.
* Walks through all in plant vessels daily verifying all work in progress and identifying and resolving any issues as they arise.
* Provides leadership and guidance to Shop Superintendants and oversees the maintenance and improvement of all shop equipment and development of shop procedures.
* Reviews and proofreads specs.

**ADDITIONAL RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Estimating as requested.
* May on occasion be required to manage a project.
* Performs other related duties as assigned by supervisor.

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

* College education and 15 years progressive experience in the maritime industry. (Apprenticeship and practical experience may be considered in lieu of a degree.) Prior management experience a must.
* Ability to estimate.
* Basic knowledge of all skilled trades, and ability to manage effectively.
* Ability to communicate effectively as a leader.

MHI Ship Repair & Services offers competitive wages and an excellent benefit package.

Affirmative Action/EOE Employer of protected veterans and individuals with disabilities.
